title: [MP][Ascend] NPU platform backends for LMCache-driven transfer
body:
Refs #4061

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Implements the Ascend NPU side of the LMCache-driven MP transfer path,
stacked on #5138 (the MLA/DSA plane-tuple format layer). All NPU-specific
kernels stay in the external `lmcache-ascend` plugin; this PR adds the
in-tree platform wiring:

- `NpuIPCWrapper`: plane-aggregating KV IPC wrapper over torch_npu storage
  IPC (`_share_npu_`/`_new_shared_npu`) — one wrapper per registered layer
  value (bare tensor or plane tuple). Device identity reuses the base-class
  UUID (torch_npu populates per-chip `get_device_properties().uuid`).
- `NpuEventIPCBackend`: torch_npu Event IPC export/import; CANN derives
  interprocess handles from the calling thread's device, so export pins the
  owning device current. Source-event liveness pinning is inherited from
  the default backend.
- `NpuCacheContext`: per-session NPU transfer resources reconstructed from
  IPC wrappers (layer groups, per-group pointer tables, temp buffers).
- `NpuDeviceOps`: `ensure_native` binds the plugin's curated
  `lmcache_ascend.ops` surface (same shape as `lmcache.cuda_ops`), with
  class-level stream-ordered recorder overrides and a view-based NPU memcpy
  (torch_npu has no CUDA host-callback primitive; libcudart cannot address
  NPU memory).
- `kv_wrap`: per-layer values may be plane sequences; the device is probed
  by descending into the first tensor. Per-layer (name, shape, dtype) log
  summary unchanged.
- `torch_ops`: `_tensor_from_npu_ptr` raw-pointer views; pointer-mode chunk
  reconstruction honors the transfer device.

Design notes: `docs/design/v1/platform/devices/npu/`.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Shared-code footprint is deliberately small: `kv_wrap.py` carries two
  functional hunks; `gpu_connector/utils.py` is untouched (per-plane byte
  geometry is supplied plugin-side).
- The NPU tests are CPU-runnable (fakes for torch_npu / acl / c_ops), so
  they run in the regular CI path.
- The plugin (LMCache-Ascend) co-develops against this branch; its curated
  ops surface is required for native binding.

**If applicable**:

- [ ] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [x] this PR contains unit tests

title: [Fix][Disk] Guard batched_async_load_bytes_from_disk against concurrent-eviction TOCTOU
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

#2420's traceback is a `KeyError` at `self.dict[key].cached_positions` after `read_file()`
silently drops `key` from `self.dict` on a `FileNotFoundError`. The reporter noted the same
pattern exists in `async_load_bytes` (now `batched_async_load_bytes_from_disk`). Open PR #4405
guards the sibling `load_bytes_from_disk`, but doesn't touch this function, so the async
prefetch path still raises the bare `KeyError` if a concurrent `remove(key, force=True)` races
its unlocked disk read.

Fix mirrors #4405 and the already-guarded `_load_chunk_into_memory`: recover the metadata under
`disk_lock` and drop the key as a miss (`ref_count_down()`, skip) instead of indexing straight
into `self.dict`.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

The race needs a second in-flight request removing the same key while this one is still
mid-read (e.g. `remove_after_retrieve` on a PD receiver, or an explicit cache clear), which I
didn't reproduce end to end through the full prefetch pipeline. The regression test reproduces
it directly at the function level with a threading barrier in `read_file`, on unfixed `dev` it
raises the exact `KeyError` from #2420; on this branch it returns cleanly.

title: Fix #5329: Reject empty slot_mapping input in parse_mixed_slot_mapping
body:
Fixes #5329

# Fix: reject empty slot_mapping in parse_mixed_slot_mapping

## What changed
- `lmcache/utils.py` (`parse_mixed_slot_mapping`): after parsing, an empty result now raises `ValueError("No slots specified")`, so it returns the standard `(None, {"error": "Invalid slot_mapping format", ...})` error like every other malformed input instead of `([], None)`.
- `tests/test_utils.py` (`test_empty_string`): updated to assert the error case instead of pinning the old `([], None)` success.

## Why
Whitespace-only (`"   "`), commas-only (`",,,"`, `" , , "`), and empty (`""`) inputs specified no slots at all but reported success. On the KVCache check endpoint those strings are truthy, so they bypassed the `if not slot_mapping` 400 guard, parsed to `([], None)`, and returned HTTP 200 with `num_chunks: 0` — while the same logical input (no slots) in another spelling got a 400. Now all slot-less inputs consistently return the invalid-format error and the endpoint answers 400.

Valid inputs are unaffected: `"1,2,3"`, `"[9,12]"`, `"1,2,3,[9,12],17,19"`, and whitespace-padded variants still parse as before.

## Verification
- Standalone check mirroring the fixed parser logic:
  - Command: `python /tmp/verify_parse.py`
  - Result: `ALL CHECKS PASSED` — `""`, `"   "`, `",,,"`, `" , , "` all return `(None, {"error": "Invalid slot_mapping format", ...})`; `"1,2,3"` returns `([1, 2, 3], None)`; `"[9,12]"` returns `([9, 10, 11, 12], None)`; `"abc"` and `"[5,2]"` still return errors.
- Syntax check on the edited module:
  - Command: `python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('lmcache/utils.py').read()); print('syntax OK')"`
  - Result: `syntax OK`
- Project suite (`pytest tests/test_utils.py -k TestParseMixedSlotMapping -xvs`) could not be run in this environment because the required dependencies (`torch`, `cachetools`, `pytest`) are not installed, so I verified the parser logic in isolation instead and kept the change minimal to the one guard plus the existing test update.

title: Fix KeyError on lookup_cache re-query after async lookup timeout
body:
Fixes #3685.

When an async lookup times out, lookup_cache() returns 0 and pops the request's
first_lookup_time entry, but leaves reqs_status[lookup_id] as None (still
pending). If vLLM calls lookup_cache() again for the same id (which happens with
nixl + enable_async_loading), it re-enters the `req_status is None` branch and
indexes self.first_lookup_time[lookup_id] directly, raising KeyError at
lmcache_async_lookup_client.py:175 and taking the vLLM worker down.

This treats a missing first_lookup_time the same as an expired one: the request
reports a cache miss (0) so vLLM recomputes, instead of crashing.

Added a regression test that drives the timeout then re-query sequence through
the public lookup_cache interface (no server, so the request stays pending). It
reproduces the KeyError on current main and passes with the fix.

title: [SDK] Query tensor capture (#4042) + fix silent query corruption under continuous batching
body:
## What this PR is

This is **#4042's work plus one correctness fix**, on top of current `dev`:

- commits `13633e4..23d08fc` are @rannnayy's from #4042 (authorship preserved), merged with current `dev` (no conflicts);
- one new commit fixes a silent query-corruption bug in the query-capture row mapping, with unit tests.

Opened as a superset so the fix can be reviewed against a tree where query capture actually works end-to-end. **If #4042 merges first I'll rebase this down to just the fix commit** — whichever is less work for you. Happy to split it either way.

## The bug

`QRingBufferCapture._build_q_step_state` maps query rows to ring slots **positionally**: it walks `metadata.requests` and advances a `row_cursor` by `op.end - op.start`. That assumes each request contributed exactly its store op's (chunk-aligned) token count of rows to the step's batched query tensor.

Under continuous batching a request's actual row count is its **scheduled** token count for the step. So any chunk-unaligned prompt tail — or a batch row order that differs from `metadata.requests` order — shifts every following request's rows, and the scatter writes **other tokens' query vectors** into their ring blocks. Silently: `retrieve(QUERY)` still returns a full-length, well-formed tensor, and the only signal is a `logger.warning`.

Minimal trigger, no decode mixing needed: request A with a 10,300-token prompt (store op covers `[0, 10240)`) followed by request B in the same all-STORE step. B's ring slots start at row 10,240; B's rows start at 10,300.

### Measured impact

Per-token-row fp64 fingerprints compared across two identical prefill+retrieve runs with a cache clear in between. Qwen3-8B, H200, `--enforce-eager --no-enable-prefix-caching`, `chunk_size=256`, prompt lengths 10159–16807:

| concurrent prefill streams | query rows identical across runs |
|---|---|
| 1 | 100.0% |
| 4 | 99.7% |
| 30 | **9.8%** |

KV was byte-identical (29/29 requests) in the same runs — KV transfers by block IDs and never touches this mapping. Layer-0 Q and K come from the same forward's hidden state, so floating-point nondeterminism cannot affect only one of them. The differing rows are not perturbed values: per-row relative deviation reaches the metric's theoretical maximum, i.e. they are **real query vectors belonging to other tokens**. Ruled out separately: incomplete `/cache/clear`, row permutation (`sort(x) == sort(y)` fails), cross-request contamination at matching offsets, uninitialized/zero slots (15615 of 15616 rows unique, no zeros).

Consequences: any query-driven algorithm computes on corrupted data at realistic concurrency — SnapKV's importance term is entirely query-driven, so ~90% of it was wrong at 30 streams — and the failure is invisible in single-stream testing, which is what CI covers today.

## The fix

Attribute rows to ops through ground truth instead of position:

- row `r` of the step's query writes its KV to GPU slot `attn_metadata.slot_mapping[r]`;
- the op's token `i` lives in GPU slot `block_ids[i // block_size] * block_size + i % block_size` (op block lists are already pre-sliced to `[start, end)`);
- intersecting the two identifies each op's rows regardless of batch composition or ordering. Each GPU slot is written at most once per step, so a full intersection is a bijection between an op's tokens and its rows.

`save_kv_layer` already receives the layer's `attn_metadata`; the connector now threads it into the dispatcher (one line). **The vLLM-side diff is unchanged.**

Behavioral improvements that fall out of the same change:

- **Mixed STORE/RETRIEVE steps capture normally.** The coarse `all(direction == "STORE")` bail-out is no longer needed — it was discarding whole steps and produced ~11.4k `Skip query` warnings in a single session.
- **Skips are per-request, not per-step.** An op that is only partially present in the step (chunked prefill split below a chunk boundary) or a ring-allocation failure now skips just that op instead of discarding requests that were already planned.
- **CUDA-graph padding rows** (slot `-1`, or rows beyond `slot_mapping`) drop out of the mapping naturally.

### Known residual limitation

An op whose leading tokens were computed in an *earlier* scheduler step cannot be captured in this one-shot design — those rows are gone. It is now **skipped with a warning instead of writing wrong data**. Fixing it properly means accumulating per-request Q across steps, which is the same machinery decode-step capture would need; noted in `docs/design/sdk/qringbuffer.md` and left as follow-up.

## Validation

- **13 new unit tests** (`tests/sdk/test_qringbuffer_row_mapping.py`), CPU-only: aligned baseline, chunk-unaligned tail not shifting the next request, batch row order permuted vs metadata order, mixed STORE/RETRIEVE, op partially present, ring exhaustion, `slot_mapping` padding, missing `slot_mapping`, no-store-ops, plus a randomized fuzz over batch compositions that asserts every accepted op captures exactly its own rows.
- Tests pass against a real `vllm==0.25.1` install as well as with a stubbed `vllm` on CPU.
- An end-to-end A/B (same box, same config, fixed vs stock) on an H100 is running; I'll post the numbers as a comment.

## Suggested follow-up

A CI regression at **≥8 concurrent prefill streams**: two identical runs, assert query tensors byte-identical. Concurrency 1 passes even with the bug, which is exactly why this survived.

## Docs

title: [MP][L2] fs_native: register persisted files at startup so restarts respect max_capacity_gb
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #5371.

`fs_native` chunk files persist across a server restart and are still served (lookup is a `stat` on the file), but the new process never registered them. They did not count toward `max_capacity_gb`, and the eviction policy never saw them, so they were never evicted. Each restart could strand up to a full cap of files, and disk usage grew without bound.

This PR registers persisted objects at startup:

- **Interface:** new `L2AdapterInterface.recover_persisted_objects() -> int` (default no-op, returns 0), delegated by `SerdeL2AdapterWrapper` and `FaultInjectL2Adapter`.
- **Storage manager:** `StorageManager` calls it for each adapter **after** the L2 eviction states have registered their listeners, both at init and in `add_l2_adapter`, and logs the count and resulting usage.
- **Native adapter:** `NativeConnectorL2Adapter` takes an optional `persisted_object_scanner`. `recover_persisted_objects()` records each object in `_key_sizes`, so eviction deletes decrement usage, and announces it through `_notify_keys_stored`, so usage counts it and the eviction policy tracks it.
  - Objects are announced newest first: LRU/ARC insert a batch in reverse, which puts the oldest file at the eviction head.
  - Keys already tracked, e.g. by a store that completed meanwhile, are skipped.
- **`fs_native`:** gains `recover_on_start` (default `true`) and a scanner that `os.scandir`s `base_path`.
  - It decodes `.data` names with the existing `fs_l2_adapter._filename_to_object_key` (the C++ connector writes the same reversible names) and takes `st_size` and `st_mtime`.
  - It registers only **regular files whose name is exactly the canonical filename of the key it decodes to**. A foreign name that happens to parse would be deleted under a different path, so it could never be evicted.
  - It skips `.tmp` files, directories, symlinks and entries that can't be `stat`-ed. If `base_path` can't be listed, it logs an error and skips recovery rather than failing startup.
- **Where recovery is skipped (warning logged).** `StorageManager` decides this on the adapter's effective (outermost) config, so wrappers such as `fault_inject`, which keep `shared` and `eviction` on their outer spec, can't bypass it:
  - `shared: true`: another live instance may be serving those files, and this process would evict them.
  - `IsolatedLRU` eviction: quotas are registered over HTTP after startup, and a salt with no quota is evicted entirely on the first pass, so every recovered salted file would be deleted.
- **`add_l2_adapter`:** recovers after the listeners and the eviction state are registered, but **before** the store and prefetch controllers can issue work against the new adapter.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- **Default:** `recover_on_start` defaults to `true`, which changes startup behaviour. If leftovers exceed the watermark, eviction runs straight after startup, and that is the point. `false` keeps today's behaviour.
- **Scan cost:** the scan is synchronous during `StorageManager` init. On a real cache of 298,492 files (849 GiB, XFS on NVMe RAID-0) it took 3.0 s to scan and ~0.5 s to register. A background scan could be a follow-up if very large directories matter.
- **Private import:** `_filename_to_object_key` / `_object_key_to_filename` are imported from `fs_l2_adapter` (lazily, like the factory's existing lazy import, to avoid a cycle). The NIXL store agents already import the same private helpers across modules. Promoting them to a public codec would touch 7 files, so it's left out of this PR.
- **Scope:** other persistent adapters (`fs`, `nixl_store`, ...) likely have the same gap. The hook is generic, but this PR only implements it for `fs_native`.
- **Validated on a real deployment.** The patch was applied to 0.5.6rc1 (commit 9a7b6050; it applies cleanly there) and the server restarted over a 911.7 GB `base_path` with `max_capacity_gb` lowered to 800:

  ```
  fs_native: found 298492 persisted objects (849.44 GiB) in /lmcache/l2 in 3.0 s (0 entries skipped)
  L2 adapter 0: registered 298492 objects recovered from persistent storage (usage 912076931072 bytes)
  L2 usage 1.06 above watermark 0.90; triggering eviction.
  L2 usage 0.96 above watermark 0.90; triggering eviction.
  ```

  - **Settled usage:** 0.86. The disk went to 738.85 GB, with 738.78 GB tracked (within 0.01% of `du`).
  - **Order:** the evicted files were the oldest by mtime.
- **Tests:** `tests/v1/distributed/test_fs_native_restart_recovery.py`, 21 tests.
  - The scanner: sizes and mtimes; skips `.tmp`, foreign names, directories and symlinks with chunk names, and non-canonical names; a listing error recovers nothing and logs.
  - Adapter recovery: usage, oldest-first LRU order, deleting a recovered object releases its bytes, no double count after a real store, and the no-scanner case.
  - Config parsing.
  - `StorageManager` end-to-end tests using the real FS extension (skipped without it):
    - leftovers are accounted, at init and via `add_l2_adapter`;
    - leftovers over the cap are evicted oldest first, waiting until the accounting matches the files still on disk;
    - `shared: true` and `IsolatedLRU` skip recovery (nothing accounted, nothing deleted), both on a direct `fs_native` spec and on a `fault_inject` wrapper around it;
    - `recover_on_start: false` leaves leftovers unaccounted.
  - I checked that each guard test fails when its guard is removed; with the `StorageManager` skip disabled, all four shared / IsolatedLRU cases fail. The `add_l2_adapter` ordering has only a functional test (its race is not reproduced deterministically).
  - **End to end:** `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_fs_native_restart_recovery_e2e.py`, 9 tests x {buffered, O_DIRECT}; needs CUDA and the FS extension. The O_DIRECT variant runs when `LMCACHE_TEST_ODIRECT_DIR` points to an O_DIRECT-capable filesystem. Each test runs the real MP server CLI (`lmcache.v1.multiprocess.http_server`) as a subprocess with `fs_native`, stores real KV blocks through the request client, restarts over the same `base_path`, and checks `/status` and bit-exact retrieval into fresh GPU blocks:
    - **Happy path:** recovered usage equals the previous run's bytes and the data is served from L2 (L1 is empty after the restart); two restarts plus re-storing every key don't double count; new writes add on top.
    - **Eviction:** restarted with usage at 0.95 of the cap, exactly the older batch (by mtime) is evicted, and the newer batch is still found and served bit-exactly.
    - **Opt-outs:** with `recover_on_start: false` or `shared: true` and a tiny cap, nothing is counted or deleted, and the files are still served.
    - **Adversarial:**
      - Foreign names, an in-flight `.tmp`, a non-canonical but parseable name, and a directory and a symlink carrying valid chunk names are ignored, never deleted, and don't stop eviction of the real files.
      - A truncated chunk file isn't served as KV data, and the server keeps serving the other keys.
    - **Known limitation:** a recovered file deleted externally stays accounted. The preconditions (stores complete, an eviction pass ran) are asserted normally; only the final accounting mismatch is `xfail`, and the test fails if the limitation goes away.
    - Each key's chunk file is recorded as it is written, rather than inferred from mtimes. The re-store test waits for the `/metrics` store-completion counter before comparing usage; I checked that it fails if re-stores charge their bytes again.
    - **Results on 0.5.6rc1 plus this change, on NVMe XFS for O_DIRECT:** 16 passed, 2 xfailed.
    - **Against stock 0.5.6rc1, no patch (buffered):** all 5 feature tests fail. The opt-out and truncated-file tests pass, as they should, since they check behaviour that matches stock.
  - Existing tests in `test_native_connector_l2_adapter`, `test_fs_native_l2_adapter_config`, `test_runtime_adapters`, `test_l2_adapter_base`, `test_fault_inject_l2_adapter`, `test_storage_manager_l2_keys` and `test_l2_adapter_factory` still pass (185 passed, 1 skipped). ruff, isort and mypy (repo config) are clean on the changed files.
- **Docs:** `fs_native.rst` states that recovery assumes this server is the only one using `base_path`, that shared directories need `"shared": true`, and when recovery is skipped.
- **Known limitations, left out of scope (existing behaviour that recovery makes more visible):**
  - A delete that reports `False` (e.g. the file is already gone) leaves the key and its bytes accounted indefinitely.
  - The `/` to `-SEP-` filename encoding isn't injective: a model name that literally contains `-SEP-` decodes to a different key.
  - Recovery's `L2_KEYS_STORED` events fire during `StorageManager` init, before the coordinator's cache-event subscriber registers, so the coordinator doesn't learn about recovered keys.
  - Very large directories are scanned into one list and registered in a single notify.
  - `fs_native`'s `relative_tmp_dir` isn't validated the way the `fs` adapter's is.
  - The `fs` adapter has the same restart gap.

title: [Bugfix][MP] Keep new L1 keys out of eviction until the L2 store rese…
body:
Fixes #5350.

StoreController learns about a freshly written L1 key from on_l1_keys_write_finished but takes its read lock later, on the store loop thread. In that window the key is resident and unlocked, so L1EvictionController may discard it; reserve_read then returns KEY_NOT_EXIST and the chunk is silently never written to L2, even when L2 has room. Under L1 pressure this shows up as persistent partial hits and re-prefill of the same tails.

Add write-back holds to L1Manager:
- register_write_back_listener(): every admitted non-temporary key reported to the listener gets one hold, taken in the admission critical section before the listener is notified.
- is_key_evictable() is false while a hold is outstanding. delete() ignores holds, so explicit deletes and post-store L1 deletions keep their behavior.
- release_write_back_holds() drops one hold per key and publishes no events. Holds are TTL locks (read TTL), so a leaked hold expires.

StoreController registers as a write-back listener and releases the holds once every target adapter has taken its read lock, and on stop for keys still queued.

The new CPU-only regression test reproduces the data loss on dev deterministically (write, evict before the store loop runs, key never reaches L2) and passes with this change.

title: [Observability][MP] Add per-backend L2 bytes-written counter
body:
Here's the PR body with the template filled in, ready to paste:

```markdown
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`L2_STORE_COMPLETED` already carries the bytes each adapter reports in
`L2StoreResult.bytes_transferred`, but only the throughput histogram used it. There was
no counter of how much each L2 backend actually writes. For flash-backed adapters
(`fs`, `raw_block`, `nixl_store` on NVMe) that is the number that determines drive wear.

This PR adds `lmcache_mp.l2_store_bytes` (attr: `l2_name`), a counter incremented by
`bytes_transferred` on each store completion:

- Failed tasks add nothing.
- Keys the adapter skips because they are already stored add nothing.

So it measures bytes the adapter wrote, not bytes LMCache offered (`total_bytes` on
`L2_STORE_SUBMITTED`). Drive writes per day for a backend on a device of `C` bytes:

```promql
increase(lmcache_mp_l2_store_bytes_total{l2_name="fs"}[1d]) / C
```

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- The metric comes from data the controller already emits. No controller or adapter
  code changes.
- It counts bytes the host wrote, not bytes the device wrote. Filesystem overhead and
  SSD write amplification are not included, so real NAND wear is higher. The docs
  call it write volume, not NAND writes.
- Adapters that never fill in `bytes_transferred` (it stays `0`) are undercounted.
  The design doc says so.
- The two zero-byte tests (failed store, all keys already stored) pass with or without
  the change on purpose. They guard against the counter ever counting writes that
  didn't happen.
- Sphinx build: 31 warnings, the same as `dev`, none in the changed files.

title: [Observability] local disk: detect, drop and count stale index entries
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`LocalDiskBackend` can list a key whose file is gone or truncated. This happens when
something other than LMCache deletes or shortens files in the cache directory
(tmp cleaners, operators, shared directories, remounts). Before this PR a read of such
an entry:

- `get_blocking`: raised `KeyError` and leaked the CPU staging buffer.
- prefetch (`batched_get_non_blocking`): raised `KeyError`, failing the whole batch.
- truncated file: `readinto` returned fewer bytes, which was not checked, so a
  **partly filled buffer was returned as a cache hit** (wrong KV served).
- all paths: the entry's bytes stayed in `current_cache_size`, so later puts evicted
  live keys to make room for space nobody held.

This PR:
- `read_file` returns whether the buffer was completely filled.
- On a missing file or short read, the entry is dropped under `disk_lock`, its space
  is released, the truncated file is removed, the controller gets an EVICT, and a new
  counter `lmcache:local_disk_stale_index_count` is incremented (once per entry, even
  with concurrent readers).
- Callers treat it as a miss. Prefetch returns the loaded prefix (matching the
  existing prefix contract in `prefetch_all_done_callback`) and releases the
  remaining buffers and pins.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Detection is lazy (on read), so the counter is a lower bound on stale entries.
- A non-zero rate means something outside LMCache is changing the cache directory.
  That is worth alerting on, because before this PR the truncated case served
  corrupt KV silently.
- Found while reviewing the same file, not fixed here (follow-up PRs):
  1. `batched_get_non_blocking` returns on a staging-allocation failure without
     releasing `disk_lock`, and returns buffers that were never read.
  2. `remove()` called outside the eviction loop never lowers `current_cache_size`.
  3. `write_file` writes in place (no temp file + rename), so a crash can leave a
     torn file.

**If applicable**:

- [x] this PR contains unit tests

title: Bound the worker adapter's _returned_finished set
body:
## Summary
This addresses part 1 of #5339 (the vLLM client-side `_returned_finished` retention). Part 2 (sidecar prefetch job / completion state) is intentionally **not** addressed here — see the issue discussion for why (native `Bitmap` memory lifecycle needs a maintainer-confirmed ownership handoff at session end before it's safe to touch).

- `LMCacheMPWorkerAdapter._returned_finished` tracks every request id ever reported as `finished_sending`, to keep `get_finished` from re-reporting an id after `finished_stores`/`previously_finished` have already been drained for it (`_update_and_get_finished_store`). That drain has no equivalent for `_returned_finished` itself, so it grows for the entire worker process lifetime.
- Fix: replace the plain `set[str]` with a small bounded LRU container (`_BoundedIdSet`, `max_size=100_000` by default) that evicts the least-recently-added id once the cap is exceeded.
- This deliberately does **not** try to answer whether vLLM's engine can re-mention an id after it's fully retired (one of the open questions in the issue) — it converts unbounded growth into bounded memory either way, at the cost of a very small, tunable risk of re-reporting an id whose entry has aged out of the cap. If that risk needs to be zero, this can be revisited once the vLLM connector contract question is answered.

## Test plan
- [x] Added `test_bounded_id_set_evicts_oldest_beyond_capacity`, directly exercising `_BoundedIdSet`'s eviction, recency-refresh, and high-volume-never-exceeds-cap behavior.
- [x] Added `test_returned_finished_stays_bounded_across_many_requests`, driving `LMCacheMPWorkerAdapter._process_finished_stores` 500 times with distinct request ids against a small cap and confirming the adapter's own set stays bounded.
- [x] Manually verified the standalone `_BoundedIdSet` implementation (identical to what's in this diff) against edge cases: single-eviction-at-cap, recency-refresh-on-re-add, and a 10,000-item high-volume load that never exceeds a 100-item cap.
- Was unable to run this repo's full test suite in my environment (native extension build for `nvtx`/nvtx-adjacent deps requires Cython, which isn't available here) - the two new tests only touch pure-Python adapter logic and don't depend on the native compute backend, so I'm confident in them from static + standalone validation, but flagging this so a reviewer can run the full suite if that matters here.

Fixes #5339 (partially)

title: fix(mp): fail closed on L1 store allocation errors
body:
##Background

This PR is aimed at resolving issue #5344. I have identified the cause of the problem: When retrieving, the determination of whether the cache is valid mainly relies on **whether the key/metadata has been published, rather than confirming that all the KV shared of TP rank have been successfully written.** 
This PR has not yet fully resolved this issue, as the problem is too extensive and requires the maintainer's confirmation before further modifications can be made. This PR is specifically aimed at addressing the issue of the release of a single TP.

## What
For the original reverse_writing function of StoreManager, it merely determined which keys failed and which keys succeeded. But in fact, there are still different states within the failed key. The modified function now carries these states instead of merely transmitting the key. In the `store` function within `lmcache_driven_transfer`, I added a piece of code to handle the `submit_callback_to_stream` for `all_dict`. This is done to clean up the staging buffers that fail halfway through.

## Why

`StorageManager.reserve_write()` filters failed reservations out of its return value. The multiprocess store path therefore could not distinguish L1 OOM from an intentionally skipped key and unconditionally reported success after iterating object groups. If a later group ran out of memory, objects reserved for earlier groups could still be committed, leaving a partial checkpoint visible.

## Scope

This is the minimal fail-closed fix for #5344. It makes each rank report failure and roll back that rank's staged objects. It does **not** implement the issue's full cross-rank two-phase commit/abort protocol; coordinated TP-wide atomicity remains follow-up work.

Existing `KEY_NOT_WRITABLE` behavior is preserved so already-resident keys continue to be skipped rather than treated as allocation failures.

## Validation

- `12 passed, 1 skipped`:
  - `tests/v1/distributed/test_distributed_storage_manager.py`
  - `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_lmcache_driven_transfer_skip.py`
- `ruff` passed on all changed files
- `ruff-format` passed on all changed files

title: feat: Add AWS Trainium device support
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Adds LMCache support for AWS Trainium via the Neuron SDK, enabling KV cache CPU
offload on Neuron hardware, including alongside Dynamo disaggregated inference in a
MultiConnector setup where NeuronNixlConnector handles prefill-to-decode KV
transfer over NIXL/EFA.

GPU code paths are unchanged from `dev`; everything Neuron-specific is in its own
module or behind a device check.

**Changes:**

- `platform/neuron/__init__.py`: Detect Neuron via native `torch.neuron`
  (SDK >= 2.27) or the legacy `torch_neuronx` shim. Adds a wrapper supplying the
  `set_device` / `device_count` / `Stream` / `current_stream` that `torch.neuron`
  lacks.
- `platform/base/device_spec.py`: New `adapt_torch_module()` hook, returning the
  module unchanged for every other backend. Neuron wraps rather than monkey-patches
  `torch.neuron`, which is process-global and shared with other libraries.
- `gpu_connector/neuron_kv_staging.py`: New. Stages selected paged-KV blocks
  between device memory and a reusable host buffer, one `narrow` + `copy_` per
  contiguous run per layer, reusing the existing CPU pack/unpack. Neuron rejects
  device→device copies between differently-sized parents
  (`nrt_tensor_copy status=2`), so the blocks cannot be gathered into a compact
  device buffer; `index_select` is avoided because it costs time proportional to
  the whole cache.
- `platform/torch_ops.py`: HND layout support (`NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_BS_HS`,
  `NL_X_NB_TWO_NH_BS_HS`), replacing a `NotImplementedError`.
- `integration/vllm/utils.py`: Force the HND layout hint on Neuron. vllm-neuron
  allocates heads-before-block-size but reports vLLM's generic NHD default, so
  detection read `NH` as `BS` and every store died on a shape mismatch.
- `integration/vllm/vllm_v1_adapter.py`: `start_load_kv` returned early whenever
  `attn_metadata` was None, which it always is on vllm-neuron — so loads were
  silently dead while stores ran. The value was never actually read. The check is
  kept for all other platforms, so CUDA is unchanged.
- `gpu_connector/{__init__,gpu_connectors}.py`: Route `"neuron"` to the paged-mem
  connectors; stream helpers that return the original `torch.cuda.Stream` /
  `torch.cuda.stream` on CUDA; devices without a pointer kernel branch out of
  `_initialize_pointers` before the pointer path, which is unchanged. Staging is
  enabled post-construction to keep it out of the shared constructors.
  `use_layerwise` and blending are rejected on Neuron.

**Two correctness fixes found on hardware:**

- Transfers are block-granular but the unpack fills only the slots it is asked to,
  so the tail block of any request not a multiple of `block_size` was scattered
  back with stale buffer contents over live KV. Unfilled staged regions are now
  seeded from the device first.
- `skip_prefix_n_tokens` was computed at both call sites and dropped on the Neuron
  path. Those tokens live in blocks prefix caching shares between requests, so
  writing them races with other requests' reads. Now a required argument.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Validated on trn2.3xlarge (single node) and 2x trn2.48xlarge (1P1D), vllm-neuron
0.24 + Dynamo, SDK 2.31, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. 1P1D needs EFA — trn2.3xlarge has
no `/dev/infiniband` and NeuronNixlConnector fails there at `agent.registerMem`.
Requires the Dynamo protocol registration from
https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/13771.

### Verified results

Staging round trip on device, compared at slot granularity
(`neuron_kv_staging_benchmark.py --verify`):

```
verify: OK -- 1199 token slots across 38 blocks round tripped exactly on 16 layers
(2 partially covered block(s) kept their unmapped slots); 474 blocks untouched
```

End to end, repeated prompt, vLLM prefix caching **off** so only LMCache can serve
the hit:

| | single node, 312 tok | 1P1D, 148 tok |
|---|---|---|
| req 1 | `computed 0, hit 0`; stored 312/312 in 187 ms | `computed 0, hit 0`; stored 148/148 in 228 ms |
| req 2 | `computed 0, hit 312`; retrieved 312/312 in 11.6 ms | `computed 0, hit 148`; retrieved 148/148 in 9.5 ms |
| TTFT | — | 0.623 s → 0.287 s (2.2x) |

`Inference Engine computed tokens: 0` is the load actually happening — vLLM
contributed nothing. Warm requests are byte-identical across repeats.

In the 1P1D column each worker stores and hits its **own** `local_cpu` cache;
prefill→decode KV transfer is NeuronNixlConnector's job, not LMCache's. Sharing a
cache *between* engines needs a shared tier (`remote_url` / the LMCache server),
which is untested here — `local_cpu` and `local_disk` both index in memory and so
are per-process.

**Three caveats worth knowing:**

1. `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` is `null` on some vLLM paths even
   when LMCache served the whole prefix. Use the `LMCache hit tokens` /
   `Retrieved N out of N` log lines instead.
2. With `--enable-prefix-caching` on, vLLM's block cache serves the repeat and
   LMCache's contribution is not separable (measured: `computed 144` of 148, with
   LMCache asked for 3). Turn it off to attribute anything to LMCache.
3. vllm-neuron pads prefill into fixed graph buckets, so loading KV does not shrink
   the prefill graph. Against pure recompute on a 1B model, offload is slower below
   ~2.5k tokens and 1.12x faster above, where the load drops into a smaller bucket.
   The retrieve is ~11 ms of a ~0.45 s request, so the limit is bucketing, not
   transfer speed.

### Reproducible configuration

Prerequisites: [vllm-neuron 0.24](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-neuron/blob/release-0.24.0.1.1.0/docs/getting-started/setup-guide.md),
[Dynamo with NeuronNixlConnector](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/13771),
2x trn2.48xlarge with EFA for 1P1D.

`/tmp/lmcache.yaml`:
```yaml
chunk_size: 32
local_cpu: true
max_local_cpu_size: 4.0
save_unfull_chunk: true
```

Single node (`NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES` must be left unset — vLLM rejects it under
its multiprocess executor, though raw torch scripts require it):

```bash
export LMCACHE_CONFIG_FILE=/tmp/lmcache.yaml
export FI_EFA_ENABLE_SHM_TRANSFER=0 NEURON_SKIP_EFA_AFFINITY=1
export NEURON_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0

python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --no-enable-prefix-caching --port 8000 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheConnectorV1Dynamic","kv_connector_module_path":"lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_connector_v1","kv_role":"kv_both"}'
```

1P1D: as above per node with `python3 -m dynamo.vllm`,
`--disaggregation-mode prefill|decode`, `--tensor-parallel-size 2`,
`NEURON_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1`, `--block-size 16`, etcd/nats on the prefill node,
and a `MultiConnector` wrapping `NeuronNixlConnector` (`kv_producer` /
`kv_consumer`, `backends: ["LIBFABRIC"]`) plus `LMCacheConnectorV1Dynamic`
(`kv_both`). Frontend: `python3 -m dynamo.frontend --http-port 8000`.

- [ ] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [x] this PR contains unit tests

title: [Bench] Neuron block KV transfer benchmark for the MP path
body:
Benchmark part of the #4864 split. Depends on #5359 and carries its commits until that merges, so the only commit to review here is the benchmark one.

Adds `benchmarks/gpu_connector/neuron_block_transfer_benchmark.py`, which times `NeuronDeviceOps.multi_layer_block_kv_transfer`. Every KV store and retrieve in the MP path goes through that one method, so these numbers are the cost of moving KV between the paged cache on device and a host chunk. The SHM writes and ZMQ round trips to the LMCache server are not included.

Measured on trn2.48xlarge, bf16, `block_size=32`, `cache_blocks=512`. Each figure is the median of 12 calls; min and max were within 1% of it.

**36 layers, 8 KV heads, head size 128**

| chunk tokens | blocks | store, scattered | store, contiguous | retrieve, scattered | retrieve, contiguous |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 1 | 1.70 ms | 1.44 ms | 1.91 ms | 1.65 ms |
| 128 | 4 | 6.80 ms | 2.53 ms | 7.29 ms | 2.71 ms |
| 256 | 8 | 12.66 ms | 4.14 ms | 13.61 ms | 4.41 ms |
| 512 | 16 | 24.24 ms | 7.04 ms | 25.89 ms | 7.23 ms |

**16 layers, 8 KV heads, head size 64**

| chunk tokens | blocks | store, scattered | store, contiguous | retrieve, scattered | retrieve, contiguous |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 1 | 0.70 ms | 0.69 ms | 0.76 ms | 0.74 ms |
| 128 | 4 | 2.78 ms | 0.97 ms | 3.02 ms | 1.05 ms |
| 256 | 8 | 5.52 ms | 1.29 ms | 5.85 ms | 1.35 ms |
| 512 | 16 | 9.88 ms | 2.04 ms | 10.67 ms | 2.12 ms |

Scattered blocks are spread across the cache, contiguous blocks form one consecutive run. The implementation issues one `narrow`+`copy_` per run, hence the 3.4x gap at 512 tokens. Scattered is the default and matches vLLM's block allocator; `--contiguous-blocks` selects the other case.

`--verify` drives a store and retrieve round trip, asserting the selected blocks return bit-exact and other blocks are untouched.

title: [Platform] AWS Trainium (Neuron) device support for the MP KV-cache path
body:
Splits the MP-mode portion out of #4864, per @maobaolong's review there. In-process mode is excluded, since that mode is marked deprecated and the review asked for it not to be submitted. The benchmark is a separate stacked PR (link added once opened).

### What this adds

A Neuron device backend so vLLM + LMCache caches KV on Trainium through the multiprocess (engine-driven) connector.

title: [Fix][NIXL] Report failed static loads correctly
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The static NIXL L2 load path previously marked present keys as successfully loaded before executing the batched transfer. If transfer preparation or execution failed, the adapter still returned successful bitmap bits and emitted L2 access notifications even though destination memory could remain unchanged or stale. A transfer failure could also leak its handle because cleanup only occurred on the success path.

- Defer load bitmap and access-notification bookkeeping until the batched NIXL transfer completes successfully.
- Release created transfer handles in a `finally` block.
- Return an all-zero bitmap and emit no access notification when batch preparation or transfer fails.
- Continue treating missing keys as individual misses without failing an otherwise successful batch.
- Add failure-injection coverage for the result bitmap, destination memory, access notification, handle release, and load completion event.

title: [Bugfix] trtllm: cap kernel object batch at 4 to match c_ops limit (#3889)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3889.

The TRT-LLM GPU connector (`TRTLLMGPUConnector._batched_transfer`) batched KV transfers in groups of `_TRTLLM_KERNEL_BATCH_SIZE = 32` object pointers per `lmc_ops.multi_layer_block_kv_transfer` call. The c_ops kernel packs pointers into a fixed `MemoryObj4` struct (`csrc/mp_mem_kernels.cuh`) and **hard-rejects any call with more than 4 objects**:

```cpp
// csrc/mp_mem_kernels.cu
TORCH_CHECK(num_objects >= 1 && num_objects <= 4,
            "Expected 1-4 LMCache objects, got ", num_objects);
```

So any store/load spanning more than 4 chunks (~>1024 tokens at `chunk_size=256`) raised `RuntimeError: Expected 1-4 LMCache objects, got <N>` and killed the TRT-LLM executor loop. Short prompts (≤4 chunks) never tripped it, which is why the existing E2E tests pass.

## Fix

- Introduce a named constant `_MULTI_LAYER_KERNEL_MAX_OBJECTS = 4` documenting the kernel ABI cap, and set the batch stride to it. `_batched_transfer` already loops with this stride, so the only effect is more (smaller) kernel launches — no semantic change. The kernel has no larger batched variant; 4 is a genuine ABI ceiling.

## Test

- Adds `TestTRTLLMBatchedTransferCap` — a **GPU-free** regression test that stubs the kernel call and drives `_batched_transfer` with 9 chunks (the failing >4-chunk case), asserting no single kernel invocation ever receives more than 4 object pointers while every chunk is still transferred exactly once.

Verified locally: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `isort --check-only`, `codespell` all clean.

title: [Bugfix] controller: parse ROUTER payload as the last frame (#3628)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3628.

With `enableController: true` and `kvaware` routing, the controller manager intermittently fails to decode worker messages on the heartbeat and reply ROUTER sockets:

```
msgspec.ValidationError: Expected `object`, got `int`   (controller_manager.py, handle_heartbeat_request / handle_batched_req_request)
Invalid ROUTER message format, expected >= 3 frames, got 2
```

Full sync never completes and kvaware routing silently degrades to session routing.

## Root cause

The controller's two ROUTER handlers read a **fixed** `frames[2]` as the payload and required `len(frames) >= 3`:

```python
# ROUTER socket: [identity, empty_frame, payload]
if len(frames) < 3:
    ... continue
identity = frames[0]
part = frames[2]
```

The worker (`lmcache/v1/cache_controller/worker.py`) is a `zmq.DEALER` that sends `[empty_delimiter, payload]` and decodes replies with `frames[-1]`. A ROUTER prepends one identity frame, so the controller normally gets `[identity, empty_delimiter, payload]`. Indexing a fixed position is brittle and **asymmetric** with the worker's own `frames[-1]` convention: whenever the empty delimiter is absent (`[identity, payload]`), the controller either rejects the message (`got 2`) or decodes the wrong frame (the empty delimiter / a non-object → `Expected object, got int`).

## Fix

- Extract `parse_router_frames(frames) -> (identity, payload)` that takes the **last** frame as the payload (matching the worker) and accepts both the 2-frame `[identity, payload]` and 3-frame `[identity, empty, payload]` layouts, raising `ValueError` only when fewer than 2 frames are present.
- Route both ROUTER handlers through it. For the usual 3-frame message this is byte-for-byte identical to the old behavior (`frames[-1] == frames[2]`); the 2-frame case now decodes instead of erroring.

The PULL/PUSH batched-push path is unchanged — a PULL socket carries no identity frame, so iterating all frames there is already correct.

## Test

Adds `tests/v1/cache_controller/test_router_frames.py` with pure-Python regression tests (real `HeartbeatMsg` msgpack round-trip) covering the 3-frame, 2-frame, extra-frame, and too-few-frame cases.

Verified locally: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `isort --check-only`, `codespell` all clean. (The function logic was also exercised directly to confirm payload selection and the `ValueError` guard.)

title: [Feat] s3 l2: support path-style addressing and key prefix (#3344)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3344.

The S3 L2 adapter (`s3_l2_adapter.py`) only supported **virtual-hosted** addressing — the bucket had to be folded into the host (`s3://<bucket>.<host>`), and object requests went to `Host: <bucket>.<host>` with path `/<object>`. Self-hosted / S3-compatible endpoints such as **Dell ECS** and **MinIO** expose a bare host and require the bucket as the first path segment, so they could not be used as an L2 backend. There was also no way to store objects under a sub-directory of a shared bucket (the issue also asked for a prefix).

## Changes

Two optional config fields on `S3L2AdapterConfig`:

- **`s3_bucket`** — when set, switches to **path-style** addressing: requests target `Host: <host>` (from `s3_endpoint`) with object path `/<bucket>/<object>`.
- **`s3_prefix`** — nests all objects under a sub-directory (`/<prefix>/<object>`), in either addressing style.

Implementation:
- A pure helper `_compute_s3_addressing(endpoint, bucket, prefix) -> (host, bucket_path, key_prefix)` centralizes resolution; `_format_object_path()` builds object paths.
- `_make_request` (HEAD/GET/PUT/DELETE) uses the resolved bucket path + key prefix.
- `ListObjectsV2` prepends the bucket path and folds the key prefix into the `prefix=` filter; `_parse_list_response_xml` strips the prefix before decoding object names (non-prefixed/foreign objects are skipped).
- **Default behavior (virtual-hosted, no prefix) is byte-for-byte unchanged** — `_format_object_path("", "", key) == "/" + quote(key)`.

Updated the L2 design doc (`docs/design/v1/multiprocess/l2_apis.md`) with an addressing section and the renamed helper.

## Tests

- `TestS3Addressing` — virtual-hosted vs path-style, prefix normalization, scheme/trailing-slash handling, and legacy-equivalence of `_format_object_path`.
- `TestS3ListPrefixStripping` — list parser strips the configured prefix and skips foreign objects.
- `TestS3PathStyleRequests` — `_make_request` produces `/<bucket>/<prefix>/<obj>` with `Host: <host>`, plus a path-style + prefix **store → lookup → load** round-trip through the in-memory fake backend.

Verified locally: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `isort --check-only`, `codespell` clean; the addressing/`_format_object_path` logic was exercised standalone (awscrt/torch aren't installed locally, so the pytest suite runs in CI).

title: [Refactor][CLI] share one HTTP helper across client commands (#3868)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3868.

The CLI client commands each re-implemented the same `urllib` boilerplate to talk to an LMCache-side HTTP server (URL normalization, `Request` + `urlopen`, JSON decode, error handling). The logic had drifted across commands, and `ping` imported `normalize_url` out of `describe` — coupling one command to another.

## Changes

New module **`lmcache/cli/http.py`**:
- `normalize_url(url)` — add an `http://` scheme if missing, strip trailing slashes.
- `DEFAULT_URLS` — default base URLs keyed by target (`kvcache`, `engine`).
- `request_json(method, url, *, data=None, timeout=10.0)` — JSON-over-HTTP transport.
- `CliHttpError` — structured failure (`status`, `reason`, `body`) raised by `request_json`.

Migrated `describe`, `ping`, `kvcache`, and `quota/_helpers` onto it. **Each command keeps its exact user-facing behavior** by catching `CliHttpError` and mapping it:
- `describe.fetch_json` still raises `DescribeError`, including the 503 `Server unhealthy: …` special case and the same connection/HTTP messages.
- `kvcache._http_request` / `quota.http_request` still `logger.error(...)` + `sys.exit(1)`, preserving their (different) error-key precedence and the `str(HTTPError)` fallback string.
- `ping` keeps its own status-based (non-JSON) probe + rtt timing, but now uses the shared `normalize_url`/`DEFAULT_URLS` — removing the `ping → describe` import.

`normalize_url` is re-exported from `describe` and `quota._helpers` for backward compatibility (existing imports and tests keep working). The bench `_normalize_url` (which also appends `/v1`) is intentionally left separate.

## Tests

`tests/cli/test_http.py`: `normalize_url`, `request_json` (success, JSON body/header/method, HTTP-error → `CliHttpError`, connection-error → `CliHttpError`), and the back-compat re-exports.

title: [Core] Support VLM-aware cache identity for vLLM MP CacheBlend
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This PR completes VLM-aware cache identity support for vLLM MP CacheBlend.

Today, MP CacheBlend can match chunks by token ids without knowing that a VLM placeholder stands for image or video content. That can make two prompts with the same text but different multimodal inputs look identical to CacheBlend. This PR gives the MP CacheBlend path a separate cache-token view that includes stable multimodal identity while keeping the raw vLLM token ids available for model execution.

Refs #2988

Summary:

- Adds shared vLLM helpers that derive VLM-aware cache token ids from `all_token_ids` plus `mm_features`, or legacy `mm_hashes` / `mm_positions`. The helpers fail closed when a request contains multimodal metadata but that metadata is incomplete or unsafe.
- Uses a dual-token view in the MP request tracker: raw vLLM token ids stay available for vLLM/model execution, while `cache_token_ids` are used for CacheBlend identity.
- Routes MP CacheBlend lookup, store, retrieve, free-lock cleanup, and L0 allocation telemetry through `cache_token_ids`.
- Gives multimodal placeholders position-aware surrogate ids and salts text after multimodal spans, so sparse/non-prefix CacheBlend chunks do not cross-match across different media.
- Adds a `tokens_u64_b64` coordinator match payload for little-endian uint64 tokens while keeping legacy `tokens_b64` as little-endian uint32 for older clients. New clients send `tokens_u64_b64`.
- Keeps non-MP vLLM V1 VLM caching fail-closed for now: VLM lookup returns no match and VLM store paths skip LMCache writes, which avoids raw-token cache pollution outside the MP CacheBlend path.
- Adds local BlendV3 and coordinator tests for VLM identity, uint64 token transport, same-media hits, different-media misses, and fail-closed cases.

Implementation map:

| Area | Change |
| --- | --- |
| vLLM integration | Builds VLM-aware `cache_token_ids` from raw tokens plus multimodal metadata. |
| MP connector | Keeps raw `all_token_ids` for vLLM execution and sends `cache_token_ids` to CacheBlend lookup/store/retrieve/free-lock/telemetry. |
| Cache identity | Uses signed-int64 surrogate ids for multimodal placeholders and salts later text tokens with multimodal context. |
| Coordinator | Adds `tokens_u64_b64` for uint64 match payloads and keeps legacy `tokens_b64` for uint32 clients. |
| Non-MP V1 | Fails closed for VLM lookup/store to avoid raw-token cache pollution. |

Scope:

This PR targets vLLM MP CacheBlend, specifically the BlendV3 CacheBlend path and the MP coordinator match path used by it. It does not add SGLang VLM support, does not add a new VLM-specific blending/recompute algorithm, and does not claim general VLM support for every MP engine path. Legacy Blend and default MP transfer paths are outside this PR's support boundary.

Coordinator compatibility note:

The current coordinator match payload for new clients is `tokens_u64_b64` (little-endian uint64). The legacy `tokens_b64` field remains accepted as little-endian uint32. Deployments that rely on VLM surrogate ids should upgrade the MP CacheBlend client and coordinator together so match requests use the uint64 field.

Validation:

- `pytest -q lmcache/integration/vllm/tests/test_mm_hash_utils.py tests/v1/test_vllm_mp_connector_mm_hash.py tests/v1/test_vllm_v1_adapter_mm_hash.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_token_hasher.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_blend_v3_load_store_opts.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_optimized_lookup_v3.py tests/v1/mp_coordinator/test_blend_client.py tests/v1/mp_coordinator/test_blend_directory.py tests/v1/mp_coordinator/test_blend_directory_api.py`
- `ruff check $(git diff --name-only dev..HEAD -- '*.py')`
- `git diff --check dev..HEAD`

Reviewer focus:

- Is signed-int64 multimodal surrogate identity acceptable for CacheBlend keys?
- Is `tokens_u64_b64` the right coordinator field shape for the uint64 match payload while keeping legacy `tokens_b64`?
- Should this PR close the vLLM MP CacheBlend portion of #2988, or should #2988 stay open for other backends, non-MP paths, or full VLM e2e coverage?

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

The implementation keeps raw vLLM token ids separate from CacheBlend identity tokens. This is intentional: surrogate ids are cache keys, not model tokens.

For non-MP vLLM V1 VLM requests, this PR chooses fail-closed behavior rather than raw-token caching. That path can be enabled later with the same dual-view model if needed.

title: [Bugfix] Persist PD transfer progress across chunked-prefill steps
body:

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Under chunked prefill, connector metadata flows scheduler → worker only.
`DisaggSpec.num_transferred_tokens` is advanced on the worker after a
successful PD store, but that mutation is not written back to the
scheduler's `RequestTracker`. The next chunk rebuilds `ReqMeta` with
`num_transferred_tokens=0`, so:

```python

becomes `min(N, 0) = 0` and the already-transferred prefix is stored/PD'd
again (or relies on decoder-side key dedup).

This PR keeps a worker-local `req_id → transferred` watermark, restores it
before the skip gate, and records it after a real store (last PP rank only,
same as today's progress advance). LocalCPU `skip_leading_tokens` is never
used to seed PD progress: a full local hit with zero peer progress must
still transfer.

title: [Perf][FS] Batch filesystem L2 I/O operations
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The filesystem L2 adapter previously awaited each key’s disk
operation serially. Batched execution should schedule independent
operations concurrently while preserving positional results and
per-key failure isolation.

- Runs filesystem store, lookup, and load operations concurrently
  while retaining direct single-key paths.
- Preserves positional lookup and load bitmaps.
- Isolates ordinary per-key I/O failures while propagating
  cancellation and other base exceptions.
- Adds tests for single-key and batched round trips, concurrent
  execution, duplicate keys, and failure isolation.

**Results (speedup = orig ÷ batched, median latency for the 16-key batch, tested on BM1743)**

***Buffered (default, page cache)***

| payload | store | load | lookup |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 128K | 2.1× | 2.1× | 1.9× |
| 512K | 3.1× | 3.3× | 2.4× |
| 1M | 3.6× | 4.0× | 1.9× |
| 4M | 6.6× | 7.1× | 2.0× |
| 16M | 9.8× | 9.7× | 1.8× |
| 64M | 12.2× | 11.3× | 3.0× |

***O_DIRECT (page cache bypassed, real disk I/O)***

| payload | store | load | lookup |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 128K | 2.3× | 2.4× | 1.9× |
| 1M | 3.9× | 3.7× | 2.6× |
| 16M | 3.9× | 3.8× | 2.2× |
| 64M | 2.6× | 5.2× | 2.8× |

**Duplicate key handling**:

- Store writes the first object for each unique key once.
- Load reads each unique key once and copies the data into all
  matching destinations.
- Each successfully populated load position is represented in the
  positional bitmap.

**Store behavior change**:

When a store batch contains duplicate keys and the first write fails,
the adapter no longer attempts a later duplicate as an implicit retry.
The original serial implementation could process the later duplicate
after the failure. The batched implementation writes each unique key
only once. This tradeoff is reasonable because filesystem write
failures are expected to be uncommon.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- The tests exercise the standard async filesystem path with
  O_DIRECT disabled.

Tested by:

```bash
pytest -q \
  tests/v1/distributed/test_fs_l2_adapter_batched_io.py
```

title: fix: apply non-deprecated config aliases instead of silently dropping them
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`_resolve_config_aliases` (`lmcache/v1/config_base.py`) only remapped a config
alias to its current key when the alias was *also* listed in
`_DEPRECATED_CONFIGS`. Every alias that lives only in `_CONFIG_ALIASES` matched
neither the deprecated branch nor the `config_definitions` branch, so it fell
through to the `else` "Unknown configuration key" branch and was **silently
dropped** (only a warning was logged, the value never reached the current key).

In `lmcache/v1/config.py` that makes ~9 of the documented backward-compat
aliases no-ops today:

- `enable_xpyd` → `enable_pd`
- `controller_url` → `controller_pull_url`
- `lmcache_worker_port` → `lmcache_worker_ports`
- `nixl_peer_host` / `nixl_peer_init_port` / `nixl_peer_alloc_port` /
  `nixl_proxy_host` / `nixl_proxy_port` / `nixl_role` → the corresponding
  `pd_*` P/D names

Setting any of these via env var, YAML file, or `from_dict` had no effect on
the intended current key.

The fix resolves each key in this order:

1. `config_definitions` first — so a name that is both a live key and a legacy
   alias keeps its current-key meaning (e.g. `nixl_buffer_size`, which is both
   a real config key and an alias for `pd_buffer_size`);
2. then `config_aliases` for **every** alias, regardless of deprecation status;
3. then keep deprecated-only keys (e.g. `nixl_peer_port`) under their original
   name for backward compatibility.

Deprecation warnings still fire independently, and unknown keys are still
dropped with a warning. The two aliases that already worked (`plugin_locations`,
`external_backends`, which are in both `_CONFIG_ALIASES` and
`_DEPRECATED_CONFIGS`) keep working.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- The change is in the shared helper, so it applies to every public constructor
  that calls it: `from_env`, `from_file`, `from_dict`, and
  `update_config_from_env`.
- New tests in `tests/v1/test_config.py::TestConfigAliasResolution` cover the
  `from_dict` and `from_env` alias paths, the deprecated+alias path
  (`external_backends`), and the alias/definition name collision
  (`nixl_buffer_size`). The first two fail on `dev` and pass with this change;
  the rest of `test_config.py` is unchanged (79 → 83 passing locally,
  `pytest tests/v1/test_config.py`).
- No behavior change for keys that were already resolved correctly; this only
  restores the documented aliasing that was being dropped.

title: [MP][Coordinator] Block startup until Kafka ingest catches up
body:
## Summary

The Kafka cache-event source (#5286) resumes after a restart from the consumer group's own committed offset. That offset and the coordinator's own checkpoint save are independent, on independent timers (offsets commit roughly every few seconds; a checkpoint every `--checkpoint-interval`, default 60s, or only at a clean shutdown). On an ungraceful crash between two checkpoint saves, the committed offset is already ahead of what the last saved checkpoint reflects — and resuming from it, as a plain consumer group would, skips the records in between for good: the broker considers them delivered, and the checkpoint that gets restored does not.

`StreamPosition` closes that gap by checkpointing the read position itself, in the same artifact as the state it describes, recording each partition's offset only after the gate has admitted that record — so a captured position can only ever lag the state beside it, never lead it. `KafkaCacheEventSource`'s `on_assign` callback seeks every assigned partition to `StreamPosition.next_offset(...)` rather than trusting the group's committed offset, so a restart always resumes from what the coordinator's own restored state proves it has seen. A partition with no recorded position (a first run, or a genuinely new partition) falls back to the group's committed offset, or `auto.offset.reset` if the group has none either — so a deployment with no checkpoint configured still gets Kafka's own best-effort resumption, just not the stronger guarantee.

That still leaves a real question once the correct resumption point is known: how far is it from the topic's tip, and is it safe to act on the fleet yet? A coordinator resuming from a real backlog restores quotas in full (metadata) before ingest starts, but the usage those quotas are enforced against fills back in only as the poll thread applies the backlog, and planning in that window compares a real limit against partial usage — ordering evictions the fleet doesn't need.

`app.py`'s lifespan now blocks on `IngestReadiness.wait_until_ready()` — serving nothing, not even `/healthz` — until the source's lag is within `--max-ready-lag` (default `1000`, Kafka-only), logging progress on a timer while it waits. Only once that clears does it start any controller. A source that can't say how far behind it is (an unreachable broker) counts as not ready and holds startup indefinitely — the safe direction, since a coordinator that has lost sight of the stream must not come up acting on a view it knows is incomplete. HTTP deployments clear immediately: their lag is always `0`.

**Revision history**: an earlier version of this PR gated each eviction sweep individually instead of blocking startup (a `GET /readyz`, an `IngestReadiness` threaded through `ControllerRuntime` and every controller) — simplified to a single startup gate, since the only time a coordinator's view is known to be partial is right after it starts. A version before that relied only on lag/readiness without `StreamPosition`, which left the checkpoint/committed-offset race above open; `StreamPosition` closes it.

Refs #4226, #4522.

title: [Fix][NIXL] Report L2 load success only after transfer completion
body:
## Problem

Fix #5325

The NIXL store L2 adapter marked keys as loaded before the DMA transfer completed. If handle creation, transfer, or cleanup failed, the load bitmap and access notification could incorrectly report success. Transfer failures could also skip handle cleanup.

## Fix

- Track the indices selected for loading.
- Release the NIXL transfer handle in a `finally` block.
- Update the load bitmap and access notification only after the transfer and handle cleanup succeed.
- Preserve correct bitmap positions when a batch contains missing keys.

title: fix(vllm): handle the vLLM 0.26.0 fused KV cache layout in group edits
body:
Fixes #4247

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`_SubpagedAttentionViewEdit` gates on `ndim == 5`. vLLM 0.26.0 registers the non-MLA KV cache as rank 4, so the edit silently stops firing and the attention group is left paged at the backend's kernel block size instead of the scheduler's. On a hybrid-Mamba model this corrupts store/retrieve with no exception and no log line. Confirmed fixed end-to-end on affected hardware — see Validation.

## Problem

vLLM 0.26.0 changed the registered non-MLA KV cache from a rank-5 K/V-split layout to a rank-4 K/V-fused layout. All paths under `vllm/v1/attention/backends/`:

| backend | 0.25.1 — `(num_blocks, 2, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size)` | 0.26.0 — `(num_blocks, num_kv_heads, block_size, 2 * head_size)` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flash_attn` | `flash_attn.py:132` | `flash_attn.py:141` |
| `flashinfer` | `flashinfer.py:392` | `flashinfer.py:408` |
| `triton_attn` | `triton_attn.py:345` | `triton_attn.py:351` |
| `flex_attention` | `flex_attention.py:133` | `flex_attention.py:138` |

ROCm AITER FA moved the same way (`rocm_aiter_fa.py:767` → `775`). The change is **not** universal: `hpc_attn.py:293` is byte-identical in both tags and still rank 5, so both ranks stay reachable and both have to be handled rather than swapped. The block dim is index 2 in both layouts, so only the rank distinguishes them.

## Effect

On 0.26.0 the `ndim == 5` gate is unsatisfiable, so the edit never fires and the attention group keeps the backend's kernel block size.

This only bites where that differs from the scheduler block size — backends advertising fixed integer sizes, where `select_common_block_size` descends to the largest advertised divisor (FlashInfer `[16, 32, 64]`, ROCm AITER FA `[16, 32]`). Backends advertising `MultipleOf(16)`, such as `flash_attn`, resolve to the logical size directly, so `shape[2] == spec.block_size` and the edit correctly never needed to fire there.

## Why it is silent rather than loud

Two guards should have caught a kernel-paged group; neither can.

At `lmcache/v1/kv_layer_groups.py:435`, `tokens_per_block` falls back to `bs` — the physical slot count read off the registered tensor — whenever the engine group info is absent or non-positive, explicitly so the group is "treated as non-compressed". The group is then misread not as compressed but as *uncompressed at the wrong block size*, so the `slots_per_block != tokens_per_block` diagnostic at `:764` never fires and nothing downstream has anything left to disagree about. (Trace credit: @MikeWang0316tw — my original read assumed the compressed variant.) And where the info is present, every check in `_validate_block_chunk_size_config` is a pure modulo test: `select_common_block_size` only returns divisors (`vllm/v1/worker/utils.py:344`), so the ratio is integral by construction, and a guard rejecting only non-integer ratios can never reject a wrong-but-integer one.

The only observable signal was the applied-edits counter missing a key — `{'mamba-page-view': N}` with `subpaged-attention-view` absent rather than zero, since it increments only on a match.

## Fix

- `matches()` — accept rank 4 or rank 5, comparing `shape[2]` against `spec.block_size` in both.
- `apply()` — handle both ranks; validate the `shape[1] == 2` invariant only where it applies (rank 5).
- `apply()` rank-4 branch — vLLM registers the fused tensor as a `permute` view of the backend's physical layout, so kernel pages tile by byte range in memory order rather than logical dim order. Reorder dims by descending stride, then check contiguity and that blocks are outermost before re-viewing; rank 5 keeps its stricter logical-order contiguity guard.

**Why patch `matches()` rather than move the edit after normalization.** The comment at `lmcache/integration/vllm/lmcache_mp_connector.py:835` states the edit must precede both group-info creation and transfer registration so they see the same edited views. `apply_kv_cache_group_edits` rebinds `kv_caches` at `:838`, and both `create_engine_group_infos_from_vllm` (`:841`) and `worker_adapter.register_kv_caches` (`:847`) read the rebound local. Moving it later would build group infos from the un-repaged tensor — precisely the bug being fixed.

## Known limitations

1. **Rank 4 under HND still resolves `block_size` to 1.** The edit machinery emits an NHD-shaped synthetic view by construction (`num_heads` is a synthetic 1), while the HND detector branch selects `NL_X_NB_TWO_NH_BS_HS`, whose `block_size()` reads a different axis. Pre-existing and orthogonal to the rank gate — it affects every edited group, Mamba included — and not reached by default, since `get_required_kvcache_layout` returns `None` and vLLM falls back to NHD. Filing separately.

2. **Rank-5 behavior is deliberately unchanged, including its `is_contiguous()` guard.** Extending the memory-order normalization to rank 5 would let a permuted tensor (vLLM ≤ 0.25.x under HND) re-view successfully and then be misread downstream as `block_size == 1` — converting a loud `ValueError` into a silent wrong block size. That is the exact failure class this PR exists to remove.

**Rollout note:** after upgrading, clear legacy L2 objects. The object key carries no layout fingerprint and the filesystem backend does not overwrite an existing object on store, so stale entries written by the unpatched code would be served as-is.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

## Validation

End-to-end confirmed by @MikeWang0316tw on affected hardware (GB10, FlashInfer, hybrid Mamba/GDN, `block_size=1600`). Stock vLLM `v0.26.0`, no local patches; two arms differing by this one file on the same LMCache build; greedy decoding verified bit-reproducible across two rounds.

| | patched | control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KV cache group edits applied` | `{'mamba-page-view': 48, 'subpaged-attention-view': 17}` | `{'mamba-page-view': 48}` |
| `Engine KV Format` | 5x `NL_X_NB_TWO_BS_NH_HS` | 4x `NL_X_NB_TWO_BS_NH_HS` + 1x `NL_X_NB_BS_NH_TWO_HS` |
| ran to `max_tokens` | 0/16 | 12/16 |
| flagged garbage | 0/16 | 2/16 |
| external prefix cache hit rate | 40–91% | 57–60% |

Both arms genuinely consumed external tokens, so this is not a no-op passing for the wrong reason.

The format row is the strongest signal and needs no generation: on 0.25.1 all five groups detect as format 2, and with this patch on 0.26.0 they do again. The fused format reaching the transfer layer is the bug's signature, not its cause — those kernels were being handed a group that should never have reached them unedited.

## Testing

`tests/v1/test_vllm_kv_cache_group_edits.py` — 19 tests, pure CPU, no GPU or vLLM install needed (vLLM and the spec-kind helpers are stubbed, and the module is re-imported under the stubs with a binding assert, so an installed vLLM cannot leak in; runs with or without vLLM present). Reverting the source fix turns 8 of them red with `assert 64 == 1600` and a log line reading `{'mamba-page-view': 4}`.

This module had no unit coverage before — testing was GPU end-to-end only, which pins faithful retrieve but cannot gate *which rules fire* for a given vLLM version. That is exactly why a rule silently not firing was undetectable in CI. The new tests pin the matching gate per registered layout and the resulting block granularity, not internal view shapes.

title: feat(mp): enable per-layer KV cache load for LMCache-driven MP mode
body:
Add per-layer (layerwise) KV cache transfer to LMCache-driven multiprocess mode so vLLM can overlap attention compute with the H2D transfer, instead of blocking on a single per-chunk (all layers per-request) transfer before the forward pass starts.

The feature is selected at runtime for CUDA. It activates only when the cache server is started with --layerwise-batch N for N > 0 and vLLM is pointed at the layerwise connector through kv_connector_module_path like below example.

lmcache server --layerwise-batch 8 --l1-size-gb 20 --eviction-policy LRU --port 5555

vllm serve --kv-transfer-config \
'{"kv_connector":"LMCacheLayerwiseMPConnector",
"kv_connector_module_path":"lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_mp_connector_layerwise", "kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"lmcache.mp.host": "tcp://localhost","lmcache.mp.port":5555}}'

Separate code path:
- lmcache_mp_connector_layerwise.py and vllm_multi_process_adapter_layerwise.py subclass the existing connector and worker adapter.
- modules/lmcache_layerwise_transfer.py subclasses LMCacheDrivenTransferModule and imports the helpers it reuses. lmcache_driven_transfer.py only does a minor change to accommodate per-layer path.
- protocols/layerwise.py declares REGISTER_LAYERWISE_IPC_EVENT_POOL and RETRIEVE_LAYERWISE for clear boundary without impacting existing request types.
- transfer_context/worker_layerwise_transfer.py and layerwise_futures.py hold the worker-side context and future.
- csrc/cuda/mp_mem_kernels_layerwise.cu holds the layerwise kernel and its launch code. The device helpers it shares with the per-chunk path moved verbatim into mp_mem_kernels_device.cuh, so both translation units include them rather than duplicating them.

Extension points added to existing files:
- LMCacheDrivenTransferModule.retrieve() routes every object-group copy through a new _transfer_object_group() hook so the subclass avoids hundreds of lines of duplicated code. The base implementation just calls transfer_kv_per_object_group in lmcache_driven_transfer.py.
- LMCacheMPConnector._worker_adapter_cls and LMCacheMPWorkerAdapter._create_transfer_context let the subclasses swap in their own components.
- server._build_modules selects the layerwise module when --layerwise-batch > 0

Multi-frame responses:
- MessagingFuture gains deliver() which reports whether a request is complete, and a blocking handler may declare a response_channel parameter to answer with more than one frame. Buffering intermediate frames and deciding when the exchange ends happens inside LayerwiseDeviceMessagingFuture.
- LayerwiseDeviceMessagingFuture intercepts frames by installing itself as the raw future's delivery sink, and that has to happen before the request reaches the wire. Add tests/v1/multiprocess/test_layerwise_retrieve_submit_ordering.py.

Layout:
PageBufferShapeDesc gains kv_interleaved. When set, an LMCache object uses the L2TD layout [L, 2, T, D] (K0,V0,K1,V1,...) instead of the default 2LTD layout [2, L, T, D] (all K then all V), so a per-layer transfer reads one contiguous span per layer. The flag is fixed at registration time to keep it off the per-request path.

Event pool:
EventPool in platform/base/event_pool.py allocates EVENT_POOL_SIZE IPC events once and exports their handles during REGISTER_LAYERWISE_IPC_EVENT_POOL, so the per-layer path signals a pooled event by index instead of exporting a handle per layer.

Mode exclusivity:
The two modes (per-layer and per-chunk) are mutually exclusive per server node, and the worker's mode is fixed at process start by the connector vLLM imports, not negotiated during registration.

title: [Experimental] Add KV compaction planning for token dropping
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Adds a pure compaction-plan builder for experimental GPU-native token dropping,
under `lmcache/integration/vllm/experimental/token_dropping/`.

Token dropping decides *which* KV entries of a request survive. Compacting the
request's paged KV then needs those positions turned into physical slot copies.
`build_kv_compaction_plan()` does only that translation:

- input: `request_block_ids`, `retained_kv_sequence_indices`,
  `current_kv_sequence_length`, `tokens_per_block`
- output: `move_source_kv_slot_ids`, `move_destination_kv_slot_ids`,
  `compacted_kv_sequence_length`

Contract: `retained_kv_sequence_indices` are indices into the request's
**current** KV sequence, not original logical token positions and not physical
slot ids. Only real copies are emitted -- an entry already sitting in its
compacted slot produces no move, so keeping everything yields an empty plan and
an unchanged compacted length.

This is the first PR of the GPU-native token dropping design; it is deliberately
much smaller than that design.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Non-goals here -- this PR does **not** move KV bytes, implement R-KV, capture
queries, integrate with the KVConnector or dispatcher, reclaim scheduler blocks,
add a config/feature flag, or touch vLLM. No torch or CUDA dependency is
introduced; the planner is integer arithmetic over block ids.

It adds only new files. No existing production file is modified.

The argument invariants are internal programmer-error checks, so they use
`assert` per coding_standards §2.2 ("Only use `assert` for development-time
invariant checks that indicate programmer errors"), not user-facing validation.

title: [MP][Bugfix] Bound client TCP connect attempts
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #4670

In MP mode on Kubernetes, the worker heartbeat can stay in degraded mode ~2 minutes after a restarted cache server is already healthy, delaying KV re-registration by the same amount. Root cause: `MessageQueueClient`'s DEALER sets no `zmq.CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, so a reconnect attempt whose SYN is silently dropped (racing the Service endpoint removal/restore during the pod restart) inherits the OS connect timeout (~127s on Linux) and monopolizes the socket — stalling every pending request, including heartbeat PINGs. Full mechanism in the linked issue.

This PR sets two socket options on the `MessageQueueClient` DEALER, before `connect()`:
- `zmq.CONNECT_TIMEOUT = 5000` ms (`CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`): a wedged connect attempt is abandoned and re-dialed within seconds instead of minutes. A healthy TCP handshake takes about a millisecond, so 5s only affects attempts that would otherwise hang. It is below the default 10s heartbeat interval, so one wedged attempt costs at most one missed ping.
- `zmq.RECONNECT_IVL_MAX = 1000` ms (`RECONNECT_IVL_MAX_MS`): zmq re-dials every 100ms by default with no backoff. This turns on exponential backoff (100ms → 200ms → … → 1s), so a down server is not re-dialed at a flat 100ms.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Per review, the timeout is now a hardcoded constant instead of a `lmcache.mp.connect_timeout` option. That removes the factory / adapter / `ExtraConfigDefault` plumbing and the docs row. The change is now just `mq.py` and one test.
- Earlier review: the `_failed_pings` counter and throttled logging were removed.
- Only `tcp://` connects can stall this way. `ipc://` and `inproc://` connects fail fast, so the options have no practical effect there.
- Behavioral check with a pyzmq socket monitor against a blackholed endpoint (SYN dropped, no RST): the stock DEALER logs one `connect_delayed` and then stays wedged. With this change it logs `closed` → `retried` at 5.0s, re-dials after 100ms, then again at 10.1s after 200ms.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` pass on the touched files.
