title: [Feature][MP] windowed kv commit policy
body:
<!--  Thanks for your contribution to LMCache!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Make sure to read the Contributing Guide before submitting your PR: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md
2. If this PR closes another issue, add 'Fixes #<issue number>' somewhere in the PR summary. GitHub will automatically close that issue when this PR gets merged. Alternatively, adding 'Refs #<issue number>' will not close the issue, but help provide the reviewer more context.-->

This is the draft implementation discussing in https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/5073

> Problem
Hybrid models (Gemma 3, gpt-oss, Command-A, Qwen3-Next, ...) have object groups that only need the last w chunks for a prefix hit (SWA, Mamba). Older windowed chunks are never read back, and they are the big ones. default writes them all to L2. But skipping them isn't enough: once L1 evicts the window, the next turn pays a full prefill. We should commit only the last w chunks, at the turn boundary.

> Proposal
Two pieces that work together: stop writing windowed KV to L2, and copy the live window to L2 at natural timing (turn boundaries) so cross-turn prefix reuse isn't lost.

title: [MP][Trace] Replay an events trace into a coordinator
body:
## Summary

`lmcache server --trace-level events` (#5312) records the cache-event stream a server emits for the coordinator, one `.lct` file per server process. This adds the other half: replaying those files into a coordinator.

- **`lmcache/v1/mp_coordinator/events_replay.py`**: `EventsTrace.load(paths)` reads one or more `events`-level files with `TraceReader`, refuses another level or an unknown `cache_event_schema_version`, and merges the records by wall-clock time (a stable sort, so a server's own `seq` order is never disturbed). `replay(trace, target, speed)` hands each record to a `CoordinatorTarget`, logging each one; batches are passed exactly as recorded. The target does what a live server would: `POST /instances` at a `start` mark (through `registrar.register`, at the recorded address or loopback), a heartbeat per registered server on a timer, one `POST /events` per batch, `DELETE /instances/{id}` at `stop`. `speed` paces by the recorded clock; `0` (default) delivers as fast as the coordinator takes batches, which is safe because the coordinator orders per emitter by `seq`.
- **Crashes.** A file that ends without a `stop` mark is a killed server or a cut recording. The replayer calls the target's `end(instance_id)` after that server's last record, which only cancels its heartbeat, so the coordinator's own `instance_timeout` retires it the way it learns of a real crash. The summary counts such streams.
- **`lmcache trace replay-events FILE... --coordinator-url URL [--speed N] [--heartbeat-interval S]`**, a new sub-command beside `replay`, which stays storage-only and untouched. A replay always registers, heartbeats and deregisters like a real fleet; the docs say not to replay into a coordinator that has the same fleet live.
- **Recorder:** the `stop` lifecycle mark now carries `instance_id` like the `start` mark does, so a file's marks stay attributable once several files are merged. Additive; the cache-event schema is unchanged.
- Docs: `docs/source/cli/trace.rst` (the `replay-events` section) and the design doc's §8, §9.8, the lifecycle record table and a §12 "Replay" subsection.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/v1/mp_coordinator/test_events_replay.py`: merge by wall clock across files, stable order at equal timestamps, refusal of a `storage` file and of a foreign schema version, delivery order and counts through a recording target (restart, stop, a stream cut without stop, skipped records), pacing, and `CoordinatorTarget` against the real app over an in-process ASGI transport (register at the recorded address, apply, duplicate counted, deregister, no port recorded, heartbeats advancing while a stream is live and ceasing at `end` so `evict_stale` retires the server).
- [x] `tests/cli/commands/trace/test_replay_events_command.py`: parser wiring, `--coordinator-url` required, exit 2 on a storage file, and an end-to-end replay through the command into the real app.
- [x] `tests/cli/commands/trace/`, `tests/v1/mp_observability/trace/` and `tests/v1/mp_coordinator/test_cache_events.py` pass. CPU only.

title: [MP] Delta-store + async-IO callbacks + LRU prefetch predictor (PR4)
body:
## Summary                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                              
   Final layer on top of **PR1 + PR2 + PR3**. Adds four independent                                                           
   improvements to the engine-driven multi-group transfer hot path:                                                           
                                                                                                                              
   - **E. Delta-Store** — prefix-based skip on `COMMIT_STORE_GROUP`. Worker                                                   
     passes the prefix-hit count from `query_prefetch_lookup_hits` as                                                         
     `skip_count`; server writes only the chunks provided at offset                                                           
     `skip_count`. For 100%-hit groups the worker sends an empty blob and                                                     
     the server no-ops the storage write — saving 14 GiB of zmq traffic on                                                    
     the re-run of a cached prompt.                                                                                           
   - **C. Async-IO MQ callbacks** — `MessagingFuture.add_done_callback`                                                       
     fires on `set_result`. Runs in the polling loop's thread without                                                         
     blocking workers on `future.result(timeout=...)`.                                                                        
   - **Server-side re-pickle fix** — `commit_store_group` deserializes                                                        
     wire format and re-pickles as `list[Tensor]` for the storage backend.                                                    
     Without this: `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'shape'`.                                                  
   - **F. Storage Batched Append observability** — `_STATS_FILE_OPS`                                                          
     counter in the server's commit paths. Tracks per-server storage                                                          
     write invocations. The actual batched-append optimization would                                                          
     require a new storage backend API (not implemented — savings <2 ms).                                                     
   - **G. Background-Prefetch predictor** — `PrefetchPredictor` module                                                        
     with LRU of `(key, hit_count, total_chunks)` tuples. Wired into                                                          
     `EngineDrivenTransferContext`. Useful for chat-session style workloads.                                                  
                                                                                                                              
   ## What's in the PR                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                              
   - **`RequestType.COMMIT_STORE_GROUP_DELTA`** — payload                                                                     
     `[key, instance_id, group_idx, skip_count, cpu_data]`.                                                                   
   - **`MessagingFuture.add_done_callback(fn)`** — fire `fn(result)`.                                                         
   - **`PrefetchPredictor`** — new module                                                                                     
     `lmcache/v1/multiprocess/transfer_context/prefetch_predictor.py`.                                                        
   - **`EngineDrivenContext.commit_store_group_delta[_raw_async]`** —                                                         
     opt-in via `LMCACHE_MP_DELTA_STORE=1`.                                                                                   
   - **`_STATS_FILE_OPS`** — module-level thread-safe counter.                                                                
                                                                                                                              
   ## Depends on                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                              
   - **PR1**, **PR2**, **PR3** — must be merged first.

`FusedRope.fused_encode()` calls `self.cos_sin_cache.to(k.device)` on every invocation.

title: [MP] Stream CPU KV events for eviction-aware routing
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Follow-up to #5076. Refs #3661.

#5076 announces completed CPU stores, but routers can retain stale placements after LMCache evicts those chunks. This PR delivers CPU/L1 store and removal events through vLLM's existing KV-event pipeline, allowing Dynamo and llm-d to update their cached-prefix placements.

For example, if workers A and B cache prefix P and A evicts it, delivery of `BlockRemoved(P, medium="CPU")` withdraws A's placement. The router can then route P to B.

LMCache MP-to-worker delivery supports gRPC and ZMQ subscriptions, without periodic KV-event fetches. 

**Event flow**:

```text
LMCache MP server
  CPU store completes / CPU chunks are evicted
                     |
                     v
                 EventBus
                     | callbacks + token/parent information
                     v
              ManagementModule
        [bounded, sequenced event log]
                     |
             +-------+--------+
             |                |
        gRPC stream      ZMQ stream
                         + acknowledgments
             |                |
             +-------+--------+
                     |
                     v
vLLM worker: LMCacheMPWorkerAdapter
  Background receiver
  [CPU event buffer + metrics]
                     |
                     | vLLM engine step drains the buffer
                     v
  LMCacheMPConnector
  BlockStored / BlockRemoved, medium="CPU"
                     |
                     v
vLLM scheduler
  Existing KVEventAggregator + ordered batches
                     |
                take_events()
                     |
                     v
  Existing vLLM KV-event publisher                                                                                                                                                           04:35:21 [28/354]
                     |
                     | ZMQ
                     v
               Dynamo / llm-d
          Update cached-prefix placements
```

**Implementation**:

- Within each vLLM engine, one rank per attached MP server opens `subscribe_kv_events`. Event callbacks wake waiting readers; idle subscriptions do not occupy ordinary request workers.
- Reuses `ManagementModule`, the existing event bus, and a bounded replay log. Completed server writes identify the chunks actually stored; store records require known tokens and parent hashes.
- gRPC uses native server streaming. ZMQ retains the subscription request ID and acknowledges consumed batches to limit in-flight responses.
- Disconnect, restart, and event loss withdraw previously announced CPU placements. Disconnects reopen the subscription. Unsupported or disabled channels retain completed-store reporting.
- Retains `KVEventAggregator` and its worker bookkeeping. Ordered batches preserve transitions such as `store -> remove -> store`.
- Exposes buffered-event count and generated, drained, received-batch, and resync counters, making a missing or slow vLLM drain visible.

The MP coordinator remains a separate consumer of storage events; it is not a forwarding hop in this path. The change stays in existing files and the MP path, with no separate vLLM patch required.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Enable the observability bus and vLLM KV events, and match hash algorithms and chunk geometry. The server retains 32,768 event records by default.
`--kv-event-log-size=0` or `lmcache.mp.kv_event_stream=false` disables the subscription. 
Both MP transports advertise `kv_event_stream`.

**Idle reception and publication are separate:** once subscribed, the worker receives events while idle, but vLLM drains and publishes them during engine steps. Router placements can therefore remain stale until stepping resumes.

This PR covers CPU/L1 events.

**Validation**:

- Selected regression: **1,497 passed, 13 skipped**.

| Routing test | MP server to worker | vLLM publisher to router | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dynamo | ZMQ subscription | ZMQ | 6/6 correct routes with full 4,000-token hits; all 9 checks passed |
| llm-d standalone EPP + Envoy | gRPC stream | ZMQ | 6/6 correct routes with full hits; all 11 routing and 7 event-accounting checks passed |

Both runs reported zero event errors. In the llm-d test, GPU copies were evicted before routing; the surviving MP server performed **3,000 L1 chunk reads**, confirming CPU-cache use. All 793 tracked LMCache Python files matched in each of the eight MP/worker containers.

Applicable pre-commit checks passed. Sphinx completed with the same 30 existing diagnostics.

The serving profile uses two independent Qwen2.5-7B engines, TP=2 each, DP=1, unsalted sha256_cbor hashes, chunk size 16, and private 2 GiB LMCache-driven L1 caches. vLLM is `0.27.2rc1.dev111+g44fc57d7b`; Dynamo uses 1.5.0 workers and the `1.5.0.dev20260821` frontend. llm-d uses unmodified EPP `b16fa8db`, Envoy `v1.33.2`, native vLLM HTTP servers, file discovery, and speculative indexing disabled.

**Follow-up work (separate PRs)**:

- Publish buffered events while the vLLM engine is idle.
- Add L2/STORAGE events, including placement ownership for shared backends.
- Support salted-hash interoperability between LMCache and routers.
- Validate Kubernetes/Gateway deployments, vLLM Production Stack routing, and additional DP/EP and multi-server topologies.

These items are outside this PR's implementation and validation claims.

title: [MP][MC][1/N] Drain admitted transfers before context teardown
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

ref https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/5030.

Series of PR for memory sharing among mp server via cxl memory.

  An MP STORE/RETRIEVE handler can still be using a registered GPU context when unregister, worker reaping, or module shutdown closes it. Protecting the initial lookup with a lock does not protect the context for the rest of the handler.

  This PR reserves context lifetime when a standard `lmcache_driven` transfer is admitted. Teardown stops new admission and waits for active handlers before closing contexts. It also:

  - Serializes registration with teardown and retains failed cleanup for retry.
  - Keeps completion dispatch alive until context cleanup finishes.
  - Releases completed handlers' admission references before IPC collection.
  - Excludes draining contexts from checksum access and retries their cleanup even after a fresh heartbeat.

title: [Bugfix][MP] End request sessions after the final STORE completes
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

A request can finish generating its answer while LMCache is still saving its KV cache (STORE). 
Today, the connector can delete the server's record for that request, called a session, too early. 
A late STORE then creates that session again, leaving it behind after the request has finished.

Keep the session until the workers report that the final STORE has completed. 
Also prevent an earlier completed STORE from marking the request finished while a newer STORE is still pending; that could let vLLM reuse its GPU blocks too soon.

```text
BEFORE: possible race
  Answer generation finishes
    -> END_SESSION removes the session
    -> Final STORE arrives and recreates it
    -> Session remains after the request is done

AFTER
  Answer generation finishes
    -> Final STORE finishes on each worker
    -> Workers report finished_sending
    -> END_SESSION removes the session
```

The answer can still be returned while the write finishes in the background. 
This uses the existing worker completion reports and vLLM's aggregation across workers.

title: [MP][Experimental] Share a fixed Device-DAX L1 pool across MP servers
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Private L1 allocators cannot safely share the same physical pool. 
This patch adds a separate Memory Coordinator that owns keys, write tokens, and offsets.
Each MP maps its host-local view of the shared Device-DAX window.
KV payloads never pass through the coordinator.

### How it works

Store one shared cache copy. Other workers reuse it.
Each MP can report to the MP Coordinator for a fleet-wide view.
It asks the separate Memory Coordinator where it can write or read shared KV blocks.

```text
FLEET VIEW (optional): registration, heartbeats, cache reports

+-------------+       +-------------------------+       +-------------+
| Prefill MP  |------>| MP Coordinator          |<------| Decode MP   |
+-------------+       | Workers, cache, capacity|       +-------------+
                      +-------------------------+

MEMORY CONTROL (required for shared L1): keys and offsets; no KV bytes

+-------------+       +-------------------------+       +-------------+
| Prefill MP  |<----->| Memory Coordinator      |<----->| Decode MP   |
+-------------+       | Keys, space, ready state|       +-------------+
                      +-------------------------+

DATA: KV bytes bypass both coordinators

+-------------+       +-------------------------+       +-------------+
| Prefill GPU |------>| Shared DAX / CXL pool   |------>| Decode GPU  |
| Host A      | write | One copy per KV object  | read  | Host B      |
+-------------+       +-------------------------+       +-------------+
```

The same MP processes appear in both control rows. 
The coordinators do not call each other in this patch; MPs connect to each separately.

- **MP Coordinator:** tracks workers and reported cache locations/capacity.
  Reports can lag. It does not allocate shared space or make blocks readable.
- **Memory Coordinator:** owns shared allocations and committed block locations.
  Every shared read checks it, even if the fleet directory reports a hit.
  Its status reports allocated pool bytes, including space no longer usable.

Fleet registration uses `--coordinator-url`; cache reports use `--coordinator-event-reporting`.
Shared-memory access uses `--l1-coordinator-endpoint`. The MP Coordinator is optional for this data path.
Keep observability enabled for cache reports.

Each MP process runs the copies for its GPU. GPU working copies still exist;
the shared pool avoids separate cached copies for each MP.
One worker pair is shown. 2P4D means 2 prefill and 4 decode workers;
4P2D means 4 prefill and 2 decode workers.

### When a block can be reused

```text
STORE
Reserve space -> Copy GPU KV to DAX -> Wait for the copy
              -> Make writes visible to other hosts -> Mark ready

REUSE
Find a ready block -> Check block metadata -> Refresh the local memory view
                  -> Check the engine layout -> Copy DAX KV to the GPU
                  -> Release the local read reference after the copy finishes
```

Incomplete writes are never marked ready. Read references keep the mapping alive until the GPU copy finishes. 
Marking a block ready is not a disk backup or a recovery checkpoint.

- Keep committed objects immutable. Never reuse extents, including aborted writes.
- Fence clients on epoch changes or ambiguous write outcomes. A persistent startup marker prevents an uncoordinated allocator restart.
- Reuse existing MP events to report shared placement and capacity once.
- Add the design in `docs/design/v1/shared_devdax_l1.md` and the setup/operations guide in `docs/source/mp/shared_l1.rst`, linked from the MP overview.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

This is an experimental TP1 path: one fixed pool, `lmcache_driven`, `noop` eviction, and a platform-qualified visibility library. It does not support L2, hybrid DRAM/DAX, GDS L1, MP P2P, CacheBlend, QStore, engine-driven transfer, or trace replay. Defaults keep private L1 unchanged.

Stop admission and drain every worker before shutdown or reset. Keep worker reaping disabled. Remove the specific startup marker only after all mapped workers have stopped. Epoch checks cannot revoke CUDA mappings. There is no automatic reclamation, persistence, HA, or restart recovery. Bearer HTTP requires a trusted network or TLS termination.

Validation:

- 285 focused and regression tests pass on the revised code.
- Changed-file checks pass, including mypy. No Rust or CUDA files changed.
- The new guide builds with Sphinx `-W` without warnings in a focused build;
  command examples, rendered links, code blocks, and design download are checked.
- Full-site Sphinx remains blocked by the same 30 warnings and one error on
  untouched base `68b7e5f5`. This patch adds no full-site diagnostics.
- Earlier hardware qualification at `9ffd4b14`: TP1 2P4D and 4P2D on two hosts, all eight P/D pairs per layout. Across MP and the corrected Maru baseline, 384 measured requests completed with zero errors, matching output hashes, and zero worker/service restarts. The hardware matrix was not rerun after this code cleanup.

Stock Maru failed correctness on that stack. Its measured baseline required benchmark-only packed-layout and CXL-visibility fixes; those are not in this PR.
The short, warm-cache results validate direct shared-CXL PD, not Dynamo routing, NIXL transfer, steady-state capacity, or production safety. Test services were removed and the original DAX bytes were restored and verified on both hosts.

title: [Perf][MP] Move LMCache-driven transfer to cudaMemcpyBatchAsync
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Adds a second copy path to the MP server's LMCache-driven STORE/RETRIEVE transfer.
Instead of staging each chunk through a GPU temp buffer and scattering it with the
block transfer kernel, eligible object groups move straight between the pinned host
object and the engine's paged KV buffers with one `cudaMemcpyBatchAsync` call per
chunk -- no staging buffer, no SM kernel. The kernel path remains the fallback and
still handles every layout.

Motivation: on Kimi-Linear-48B (TP 2, 1024-token MLA pages, 128k prefix) an nsys A/B
shows the kernel path's scatter kernels each waiting ~1.6 ms to be scheduled on a GPU
busy with vLLM's prefill -- about 50 ms of stream idle per 128k retrieve -- while the
copies themselves already ran at line rate. With 1024-token MLA pages each
(layer, block) of a chunk is a contiguous ~1 MB run, so the copy engine can move it
directly and the SMs are left to vLLM.

Changes:

- `csrc/cuda`: `execute_direct_copy_transfer`, `batch_memcpy_supported`,
  `direct_copy_format_supported`, plus the `DirectCopyGroupSpec` / `DirectCopyObject`
  descriptors. One `resolve_block_addressing` switch turns each eligible
  `EngineKVFormat` into a base-pointer rule and three byte strides, mirroring
  `calculate_engine_global_offset` (including the padded `block_stride_elems` of
  pool-shared MLA rows), so the per-entry loop has no format branches. Host ranges are
  split at `LazyMemoryAllocator.PIN_CHUNK_SIZE` boundaries, since each pin chunk is a
  separate `cudaHostRegister` region. Requires CUDA runtime and driver >= 12.8;
  compiled out on HIP.
- `object_group_transfer.py`: `_HAS_BATCH_MEMCPY_ASYNC` resolves build- and
  driver-level support once at import; `direct_transfer_supported` then checks each
  object group (host block ids present, no GDS-backed object, every kernel group on a
  token-major layout whose paged block is one contiguous run).
  `transfer_kv_per_object_group` consults both before the staged fast path and hands
  eligible groups to `run_direct_transfer`, which mirrors the staged planner's window
  and `skip_first_n_tokens` logic. Ineligible layouts (HND, blocked-scale,
  (K,V)-tuple), GDS objects and older builds fall back to the kernel path; an
  ineligible layout is logged once per format.
- `transfer_kv_per_object_group` gains `block_ids_host`, the host-list view of the
  same downsampled ids already passed as device tensors. The direct path resolves
  every address on the CPU; callers that must stay on the kernel path leave it empty,
  which is how `qstore` keeps its current behaviour.
- `BaseCacheContext.get_kernel_group_offset_in_object` and
  `get_kernel_group_kv_pointer_list` (the latter cached on `GPUCacheContext` so it
  does not sync the stream).
- Torch fallbacks for the two new query functions, keeping `test_cuda_ops_parity`
  green.

There is no configuration flag: the direct path is taken automatically whenever the
build, the driver and the layout allow it, and falls back otherwise.


**If applicable**:

- [x] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [x] this PR contains unit tests
  - `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_direct_copy_transfer_gpu.py`: bit-exact parity with
    the kernel path for every eligible format, both directions, a skipped block

title: feat: add native 3FS (HF3FS) L2 storage backend
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a **native C++ 3FS (Fire-Flyer File System) L2 storage backend** to LMCache,
giving it high-performance distributed KV-cache storage backed directly by the
3FS **Usrbio** API.

### What this PR does / why we need it

- **What:** A complete 3FS storage backend stack — a native C++ connector, a pybind wrapper,
  a Python L2 adapter (config + factory registration), a build profile, unit/integration tests,
  and user documentation.
- **Why:** 3FS (from DeepSeek) is a high-performance distributed file system well suited
  to large, warm/cold KV-cache tiers and cross-node cache sharing. LMCache previously had no
  native 3FS backend; KV caches had to go through slower, higher-latency paths. By performing
  I/O through the 3FS Usrbio API with **GIL-free, multi-worker parallel read/write**, this PR:
  - Reduces TTFT on cold-cache misses.
  - Increases throughput for large KV caches via batched ops and multi-path balancing.
  - Provides accelerated `EXISTS` checks without hitting the filesystem (in-memory key buffer).

## How it works

The feature is layered; each layer only exposes a narrow public interface:

```
                    Hf3fsL2AdapterConfig + factory "hf3fs"
                                   │
                    hf3fs_l2_adapter.py (NativeConnectorL2Adapter)
                                   │
                    lmcache_hf3fs CppExtension (pybind.cpp → LMCacheHf3fsClient)
                                   │
                    Hf3fsConnector (connector.h/.cpp)  ── 3FS Usrbio API
```

1. **Native connector** `csrc/storage_backends/hf3fs/connector.{h,cpp}`
   - `Hf3fsConnector : ConnectorBase<WorkerHf3fsConn>` implements
     `do_single_get/set/exists/delete` and `do_batch_exists`.
   - **Per-worker connection state** (`WorkerHf3fsConn`) keeps **dual Ior + dual Iov**
     (separate read/write rings) per thread. Separate Ior are required because the 3FS Ior
     cannot handle read and write operations simultaneously; per-thread Iov avoids
     synchronization and IB-registration complexity.
   - **Multi-path load balancing:** objects are distributed across the configured
     `base_paths` based on `chunk_hash`.
   - **Accelerated `EXISTS` (key buffer):** an in-memory `sharded_flat_hash_set<std::string>`
     (built on `absl::flat_hash_set`, with per-shard locks for high write throughput) is
     populated once by scanning the base paths at startup. `do_batch_exists` then answers from
     the buffer without touching 3FS, only falling back to the FS when the buffer is disabled.
   - **Per-op worker lanes:** optional `per_op_workers` (`lookup/retrieve/store/delete`) via
     `WorkerPoolConfig` for isolated worker pools per operation class.

2. **Pybind:** `pybind.cpp` exposes the connector through a `LMCacheHf3fsClient` module.

3. **Python adapter:** `hf3fs_l2_adapter.py` adds `Hf3fsL2AdapterConfig` and registers the
   `"hf3fs"` adapter type + factory, backed by the existing `NativeConnectorL2Adapter`.

4. **Build profile:** `hf3fs.py` builds `lmcache.lmcache_hf3fs` when `BUILD_HF3FS=1`, linking
   against `libhf3fs_api_shared` and the system Abseil libs
   (`absl_hash`, `absl_city`, `absl_int128`, `absl_raw_hash_set`); Abseil availability is
   detected before building.

### Configuration example

```
[lmcache]
type = "hf3fs"
mount_point = "/3fs/stage"
base_paths  = "/3fs/stage/lmcache/p1,/3fs/stage/lmcache/p2"
num_workers = 8
# optional tunables:
ior_entries     = 256     # [128, 1024]
io_depth        = 0       # [-128, 128]
iov_size        = 209715200  # 200 MB, [100MB, 2GB]
enable_key_buffer = true
# per_op_workers = {"lookup": 2, "store": 4}
```

### Dependencies & build

- Requires the **3FS Usrbio SDK** (`hf3fs_usrbio.h`, `libhf3fs_api_shared.so`) and system
  **Abseil** (`libabsl-dev`).
- Build:
  ```bash
  export HF3FS_INCLUDE_DIR=/usr/include
  export HF3FS_LIB_DIR=/usr/lib
  BUILD_HF3FS=1 pip install -e . --verbose
  ```

### Testing

- `tests/v1/distributed/test_hf3fs_l2_adapter.py`
  - Config/validation tests (ranges, mount/base-path checks, per-op workers, key-buffer).
  - Native-connector tests: client creation, single/batch put-get roundtrip, exists, delete,
    multi-path distribution, persistence across clients.
  - L2-adapter integration: store/lookup, load, delete, end-to-end workflow, multi-object batch.
- Result on a live 3FS mount (`HF3FS_MOUNT_POINT=/3fs/stage`): **33 passed, 1 skipped**
  (the skipped case is the "extension absent" failure-path test).

### Notes for reviewers

- New public API is minimal: one connector class + one adapter config/factory.
- Files: `csrc/storage_backends/hf3fs/*`, `hf3fs_l2_adapter.py`, `hf3fs.py`,
  `test_hf3fs_l2_adapter.py`, `docs/source/mp/l2_storage/{hf3fs.rst, supported_storages.rst,
  remote_and_distributed.rst}`.

Signed-off-by: Ruyi Zhang <ruyi.zhang@samsung.com>
Co-authored-by: Wenwen Chen <wenwen.chen@samsung.com>

title: feat(nixl): add IBM_SCALE backend support and fix NIXL transfer performance
body:
Add IBM Storage Scale (`IBM_SCALE`) to all NIXL backend allowlists and fix
several performance bugs in the NIXL transfer path that are exposed by
`io_uring`-backed backends (IBM_SCALE, GDS).

1. Add IBM_SCALE to allowlists
   - `nixl_store_dynamic_l2_adapter.py`: `_VALID_DYNAMIC_BACKENDS` (via `FILE_DYNAMIC_BACKENDS`)
   - `nixl_store_l2_adapter.py`: `_VALID_NIXL_BACKENDS`, `_FILE_BACKENDS`

2. Fix 10 ms polling floor in `post_non_blocking` / `_post_non_blocking`
   Add a 20-iteration spin-check before falling back to a 1 ms cooperative
   sleep. Move the sleep before `check_xfer_state` so a transfer completing
   on the first poll exits immediately without paying an extra sleep.
   Eliminates the ~10 ms floor that dominated latency for `io_uring` backends.

3. Concurrent store via `asyncio.gather` in `_execute_store_in_the_loop`
   Reserve all keys under the lock first, then launch all
   `dynamic_store_file` coroutines concurrently. Per-key failure isolation
   via `return_exceptions=True`. Matches the existing concurrent load path.

4. Fix `_open_flags()`: `O_RDWR` → `O_WRONLY` (store) / `O_RDONLY` (load)
   `O_RDWR` is ambiguous for backends that infer write intent from the fd
   access mode (IBM_SCALE uses this to select the right GPFS prefetch
   hint). `O_WRONLY`/`O_RDONLY` is also better POSIX practice.

5. Move `os.stat` outside the lock in secondary lookup
   `_secondary_lookup_locked` called `os.stat` while holding `_lock`,
   blocking concurrent store/load on slow/remote filesystems. Refactored
   to a two-lock, one-stat pattern: collect missing keys under lock, stat
   them unlocked, then commit found entries under lock. Removes
   `_secondary_lookup_locked` entirely.

Refs: ai-dynamo/nixl#2134

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Enables `IBM_SCALE` as a valid backend in LMCache's static and dynamic NIXL
adapters. Without this, LMCache raises a `ValueError` at config validation
time even when the IBM_SCALE plugin is installed. The accompanying
performance fixes (items 2–5) benefit all fast `io_uring` backends — GDS
users also see reduced TTFT.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Items 2–5 are independent of IBM_SCALE and improve the general NIXL transfer
  path. They can be reviewed/merged separately if preferred.
- The companion upstream NIXL plugin PR is ai-dynamo/nixl#2265.

title: [good-first-issue] distributed: convert f-string log calls to %-format
body:
Follow-up step for the G004 rollout in #5118. #5125 enabled `G004` repo-wide with temporary `per-file-ignores` for the not-yet-migrated files, and the plan agreed there is to remove those entries directory by directory as each area is cleaned up.

This does that for `lmcache/v1/distributed/`, the last two files under it that were still ignored:

- `l2_adapters/bigtable_l2_adapter.py` (5 call sites)
- `transfer_channel/impl/mooncake_te_impl.py` (4 call sites)

and deletes both `per-file-ignores` entries, so the directory can no longer regress. Together with `lmcache/v1/multiprocess/` (already clean), both directories that enforce SLF now enforce G004 as well.

Format style only, no behaviour change. Format specifiers were chosen from each variable's type annotation per `docs/coding_standards.md` 7.4:

| Variable | Source of truth | Spec |
|---|---|---|
| `qual` | key of `shards_raw: dict[str, tuple[bytes, int]]` | `%s` |
| `ts`, `max_ts` | `int` value slot of that dict (`cell.timestamp_micros`) | `%d` |
| `(max_ts - ts) / 1e6` | true division, original used `:.2f` | `%.2f` |
| `key_str`, `rk_str` | `.decode("utf-8")` | `%s` |
| `size` | `len(obj.byte_array)` | `%d` |
| `limit_bytes` | `int(...)` | `%d` |
| `column_name` | `column_name: str = "data"` | `%s` |
| `_remote_session_id` | ctor param `remote_session_id: str` | `%s` |
| `batch_id` | key type of `self._tasks: dict[int, tuple]` | `%d` |
| `advertise_host` | `@property -> str` | `%s` |
| `mooncake_te_port`, `get_rpc_port()` | `@property -> int` | `%d` |
| `_protocol`, `_device_id` | `collect_env_var() -> tuple[str, str]` | `%s` |

All nine messages render byte-identically to the f-strings they replace.

Two details worth flagging for review:

- In `"...diff is %.2fs)"` the trailing `s` is a literal second-unit suffix, not part of the specifier.
- `get_rpc_port()` is intentionally left as a call in the argument list. Lazy formatting defers interpolation, not argument evaluation, so this preserves the existing behaviour rather than making an unrelated change.

One message changed shape but not content: the `Column ... not found in row ...` warning previously split mid-phrase across two implicitly concatenated literals. Dropping the `f` prefixes freed enough width to fit a single literal within 88 columns, matching the already-converted call a few lines above it. Every other implicit concatenation is preserved as-is.

## Testing

- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean; `isort`, `codespell` and `mypy --config-file=pyproject.toml` clean on the changed files.
- `ruff check --isolated --select G004 lmcache/v1/distributed/` now reports 0 findings (was 9).
- Verified the ignore removal is effective rather than cosmetic: a temporary `logger.info(f"...")` added to `bigtable_l2_adapter.py` is reported as `G004` with this change and passes without it. Probe removed afterwards.
- `pytest tests/v1/distributed/` gives 790 passed, 80 skipped on a CPU-only build (`NO_GPU_EXT=1 pip install -e . --no-build-isolation`, torch 2.14.0+cpu, Python 3.12). `tests/v1/distributed/test_bigtable_l2_adapter.py` gives 14 passed.
- Because `PLE1206` (too-few logging args) is not in `select`, a dropped argument or wrong specifier would only surface at runtime, so each of the 9 sites was additionally rendered both ways with representative values and compared: all 9 identical.

title: [Feat][MP] Engine-driven multi-group transfers via KVLayerGroupsManager
body:
Rebuilt along @ApostaC's three steps, on top of #4079 (first commit is that move; it drops out when #4079 merges):

1. Registration initializes `KVLayerGroupsManager` and derives every group's geometry from it (no per-group re-detection). The manager also validates chunk and window divisibility.
2. Block IDs are parsed per group from the manager's kernel groups; sliding-window groups keep only the trailing window of each chunk.
3. Gather/scatter call the shared helpers moved in #4079, extended with `blocks_per_window`.

The chunk token count is `blocks_in_chunk * lcm(group block sizes)`, folding in the mixed-geometry fix @skaulintel found on the old branch (gemma-4 registered half of every chunk). Covers both transports: SHM reserves per-group slots, pickle sends a group-major payload. k3 lanes: kimi_linear_tp and engine-driven HMA lm-eval, both transports.
